title: Everything streams
summary: The game now plays in a browser and on phones as well as on Linux and Windows, and nothing makes you wait. There are no loading screens: the title opens at once and everything loads behind play, every sprite first as a procedural placeholder of simple shapes in its own colours, then its real picture. Planets are made chunk by chunk round you, a solar system streams in piece by piece nearest first, and every planet's surface is built ahead in the background so landing takes only the animation. One memory pool holds every loaded asset, unloading the least used only when it runs out of room, and a loading console above the event log shows the work, the pool and a map of its memory. The hull and shield bars became a liquid-filled gauge of your ship's outline inside a shield ring, with afflictions round it, and the automaton gained a shield of its own.

steps.title: In a browser and on phones
steps.text: The game now exports for the web (itch.io), Linux and Windows. In a browser and on phones it runs on the Compatibility renderer (WebGL 2), with threads for smooth planets and its own sound mixing so audio plays. A touch screen gets buttons by the left edge (menu, computer, map, attack, dock, zoom); a tap is a click, a two-finger tap a right click, a pinch zooms. The web build carries half-size anatomy pictures: 214 MB of data down to 153 MB.

steps.title: No loading screens
steps.text: The game opens straight on the title screen and loads everything else behind it. A new game, a loaded save and Talos open at once; the economy warms up a little a frame while you play. In a browser the title shows in about a second (it was 17 to 65 seconds) and you fly about 2 seconds after START GAME (was 9).

steps.title: Procedural placeholders first
steps.text: Every sprite gets a procedural placeholder before any picture loads: a simple shape for its kind (a hull with swept wings, a station ring, a beast, a figure, a building block, a glow...) in the sprite's own two colours, fitted to where its picture is opaque. All 1093 are made in well under a second; only then do the real pictures load, each replacing its placeholder in place.

steps.title: Planets made chunk by chunk
steps.text: A planet is no longer made all at once. The new planner makes it as units that come out the same in any order: terrain in blocks, the plan of villages, gates and industry, then 32 x 32 tile chunks with their ramps, tiles and creatures. Chunks stream in on a worker round you, nearest first, over a plate of the ground's colour, taken in within 2.5 ms a frame.

steps.title: A solar system streams in
steps.text: Entering a system no longer stops the game while it is built. Only the core (your ship, the HUD) is made first; the planets, moons, stations, gates, ships, monsters and asteroid fields are a queue of pieces made nearest to you first, as many a frame as fit in 2.5 ms, each fading in. A new game is still for 150 ms (it was 595).

steps.title: Every planet's surface built ahead
steps.text: Every landable planet of a system has its surface built in the background as you fly, one at a time, nearest first, so landing takes only the landing animation. A finished surface is set aside out of the scene (parked), so it costs nothing while you fly; landing puts it back in about 9 ms. In a browser the nearest three are built.

steps.title: A memory pool
steps.text: Every loaded asset is in one memory pool with its size: the sprites, their picture data, the anatomy pictures, the placeholders and the surfaces built ahead. Nothing is unloaded unless the pool runs out of room, which is twice what the game usually needs. Each use raises an asset's priority (fading with a 5-minute half-life); when room runs out, the least used ones nothing holds are unloaded first, and each unload is reported.

steps.title: The loading console and the memory map
steps.text: Above the event log, the loading console shows what is loading and being made, with a scroll bar over the last 1000 lines, the memory pool's total, a progress bar and the memory map: the pool's room as a strip, each kind of asset an area as wide as its memory in its own colour. Hovering an area lists its biggest assets with their size and priority. The arrow folds the console to the bar alone.

steps.title: The health gauge
steps.text: The hull and shield bars are replaced by a gauge: your ship's own outline, filled with red liquid to the hull's share (a moving wavy surface, a bright waterline and rising bubbles), inside a ring of blue liquid filled to the shields' share. Afflictions sit round the ring as icons, clockwise from the top, with the numbers below.

steps.title: The automaton's shield
steps.text: On foot, the automaton now has a shield of 40 (more with gear). It takes a hit before your health and your parts, and recharges 12 a second once you have been out of the fight for 3 seconds. The surface HUD shows the same gauge with the automaton's outline.

diagram.text: after 3 s out of the fight

steps.title: Fixes
steps.text: Nebulae no longer pop in and out as you fly (their layer stopped repeating). The game no longer crashes as it closes. The mining panel shows only while you mine. The title screen no longer flashes asteroids at the first start. Players' builds start without the FPS meter. Quitting while a planet is being made no longer hangs.

review.intro: Patch 0014 in code: web, Linux and Windows exports with touch controls (export_presets.cfg, project.godot, touch_controls.gd, settings.gd); no loading screens - the title first, everything else behind play (main_menu.gd, load_veil.gd, galaxy.gd, loading_screen.gd removed); procedural placeholders for every sprite before the pictures (placeholder_art.gd, proc_art.gd, tools/sprite_sizes.py, data/sprites/sizes.json); planets made chunk by chunk (surface_planner.gd, planet_surface.gd, ground_chunks.gd); a solar system streamed in as a queue of pieces and every planet's surface built ahead and parked (main.gd, bg_work.gd); the memory pool (asset_pool.gd) and the loading console with its memory map (event_log.gd); the liquid health gauge and the automaton's shield (health_gauge.gd, gauge_fill / gauge_ring shaders, hud.gd, surface_props.gd); and fixes (main.tscn's nebulae, ui.gd's dismantling, mining_panel.gd, warmup.gd). Tests: test_asset_pool, test_touch, test_play's streaming and built-ahead checks, and hp + shield comparisons across the suite.

The player's guide (F1). It now explains the new streaming: the loading console with its memory pool and memory map, systems streaming in, planets built ahead and made chunk by chunk. It also covers playing by touch, the health gauge with its shield ring, the automaton's shield, and the FPS counter being off by default in released builds.

Laser bolts and arrows are fast and home in on their target: you can't outrun or dodge them - fight back, or get out of range before they fire. Fight them yourself: click one (or press F). files.explanation: New data file written by tools/sprite_sizes.py. For each of the game's 1093 sprites it stores the size, two main colours and the box its opaque part fills. ProcArt uses it to make a placeholder for a sprite before the real picture is loaded: PlaceholderArt draws a simple shape of the right kind, in the sprite's colours, fitted to that box.

hunks.title: Every sprite's size and colours
hunks.note: One compact line: each key maps to [w, h, main colour, shade, x0, y0, x1, y1]. The colours are the mean of the opaque pixels and of their darker half. The box is in hundredths of the width and height. The placeholder therefore has the real sprite's size, colours and outline, and swapping in the picture doesn't move anything.

New working document (outside the game; external/ is not exported) for the real-time plan: nothing ever blocks the player. It lists the principles, the stages (chunked planets, streaming systems, heavy one-off screens) and a progress log, so the work can carry on across sessions.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,57 @@ # Real-time, modular architecture - the plan 
+# Real-time, modular architecture - the plan (working document)
+
+Goal (the user, 2026-11-20): nothing ever blocks the player. Everything is made of small
+components assembled into bigger ones; every operation takes a fraction of a second of a frame
+(time-sliced on the main thread, the heavy part on worker threads); what isn't ready yet shows as
+a placeholder and is replaced as soon as it is - chunk by chunk, for planets and solar systems.
+
+## Principles
+1. Work units: a job is small (a chunk, a region's plan, a picture) - < ~30 ms on a worker in a
+   browser, its result taken in on the main thread within a per-frame budget (a few ms).
+2. Streaming by need: what's near the player first, outward; far things later or never.
+3. Placeholders everywhere: a sprite (ProcArt.sprite), ground (a flat plate of the planet's
+   ground colour), a building or a creature not out yet - the real thing replaces it in place.
+4. Nothing waits: no loading screen, no "wait for all X"; gameplay works on what's there
+   (ungenerated ground isn't walkable yet; it's generated before you can reach it).
+5. Deterministic per unit: a chunk or a region generates the same from its seed, in any order.
+
+## Stage 1 - the planet surface, chunked (done 2026-11-20)
+Units:
+- Planet constants (once, fast): noise objects, the water shape's parameters (drawn from the
+  planet's rng), the height normalisation (lo/hi from a coarse 1/8 sample of the whole planet),
+  the site height (commonest walkable band, same coarse sample).
+- Region plan (REGION 110 tiles; the pad's own plan first): raw terrain of the region (+margin),
+  then its village (palace, houses, plots levelled, citizens), pirate band, wild gate, industry
+  sites (gas giant), fauna - each from a seed of (planet, region). Its edits (levelled plots,
+  discs, clear spots) are what chunks apply.
+- Gen chunk (GEN 32 tiles = 2 scenery chunks): raw terrain of chunk + margin, the edits of the
+  regions it overlaps, terrain bands, crags closed, tile levels (smoothed 3x3 twice), plots and
+  spots levelled, natural ramps (hash), linking ramps inside the chunk (BFS: every level component
+  linked where a ramp fits), islands' causeways (a deterministic lattice), the chunk's tiles
+  (TileMapLayer cells per level), its map pixels (hill-shaded), its ground_data. On a worker;
+  returned as chunk-local arrays; copied into the planet's N x N arrays on the main thread.
+- Streaming: chunks ordered by distance to the pilot (the pad's first); a few on workers at once;
+  taken in within ~3 ms a frame; scenery, buildings, gates, creatures and people only where their
+  chunk is in; the ground pictures (GroundChunks) redrawn where a chunk lands.
+- Placeholder ground: the planet's ground colour as a plate under everything, real tiles over it
+  as their chunks come.
+- The surface opens at once (no build to wait for); landing = the animation only.
+
+## Later stages
+2. Solar systems: every system piece (planets, stations, belts, ships) a component made in slices
+   as it comes into range; nothing built whole on arrival.
+3. Other heavy one-off work (Ship Computer pages, Talos screens, galaxy generation) - the same
+   pattern: a job queue with a frame budget.
+
+## Progress log
+- 2026-11-20: plan written; reading the surface's consumers of the planet arrays.
+- 2026-11-20: stage 1 done - SurfacePlanner + streaming in planet_surface.gd; full suite green (stream_all in the
+  whole-planet tests). Next: the asset memory pool (priority by use, budget 2x need, unloads reported) and the
+  loading console; then stage 2.
+- 2026-11-20: memory pool (AssetPool) + loading console done; suite 298 green. Next: stage 2 (solar systems in
+  slices), then the heavy one-offs (Ship Computer first open, Talos, galaxy generation); re-measure FPS on a quiet
+  machine (the last tour ran beside another game: surfaces 20-35% under baseline, not trustworthy).
+- 2026-11-20: stage 2 done - a system's pieces stream in nearest first (main.gd _piece queue), the scene live
+  after ~150 ms; every landable surface built ahead and pooled; console scrolls/folds, memory map. Another
+  session works on ui.gd dismantle, warmup.gd, the Ship Computer / Talos first opens (stage 3) - main.gd and
+  event_log.gd are this session's.
hunks.title: The plan
hunks.note: It sets out five principles: small jobs, streaming nearest first, placeholders everywhere, nothing waits, and units that are deterministic from their seed. It describes stage 1, the chunked planet (constants, region plans, 32-tile generation chunks, streaming, the placeholder plate), and the later stages for systems and one-off screens. The progress log marks stage 1, the memory pool and stage 2 as done.

files.explanation: New file. AssetPool is the memory pool for loaded assets: sprites, their CPU copies, the anatomy pictures, the placeholders, and planet surfaces built ahead. Nothing is unloaded unless the pool runs out of room. The room is twice the usual need. Each asset's priority counts its uses, fading with a 5-minute half-life. When the pool is over budget, it unloads the least-used assets that nothing holds. Every load and unload is noted for the loading console, and breakdown() feeds its memory map.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,224 @@ 
+class_name AssetPool
+extends RefCounted
+## The memory pool of the game's loaded assets (the sprites, their CPU copies,
+## the automaton's anatomy pictures). What's loaded stays loaded: nothing is
+## unloaded unless the pool runs out of room. Its room (budget) is twice what
+## the game usually keeps loaded (need: every sprite, the anatomy pictures) -
+## to be on the safe side.
+##
+## Each asset has a priority from how much it's used: every use (touch) adds
+## one, and the count fades with a half-life (HALF_LIFE) - what you use now
+## outranks what you used an hour ago. Over budget, the lowest-priority assets
+## that nothing else holds (a sprite on screen holds its texture) are unloaded
+## until it fits; pinned ones (costly to load again) never are. An unloaded
+## asset comes back when it's next asked for (a placeholder until then).
+##
+## Every load and unload is noted (events: the loading console above the event
+## log shows the latest, and the pool's total).
+
+const HALF_LIFE := 300.0          # s
+const KEEP_EVENTS := 1000
+
+class Entry:
+	var key := ""
+	var label := ""
+	var bytes := 0
+	var uses := 0.0               # (as of `at`: fades from then)
+	var at := 0.0                 # s, the last use
+	var unload: Callable          # drops the asset (its owner forgets it)
+	var held: Callable            # true while something else holds it (can't be freed)
+	var pinned := false
+
+static var _e := {}               # key -> Entry
+static var used := 0              # bytes loaded now
+static var need := 0              # bytes the game usually keeps loaded
+static var budget := 0            # bytes: 2 x need (set_need), or set directly (tests)
+static var peak := 0
+static var loads := 0
+static var unloads := 0
+static var unloaded_bytes := 0
+## The latest notes: [seconds, text, kind ("load", "unload", "work")]; `serial` counts them all.
+static var events: Array = []
+static var serial := 0
+
+
+static func _now() -> float:
+	return Time.get_ticks_msec() / 1000.0
+
+
+## What the game usually keeps loaded (bytes): the room is twice that.
+static func set_need(bytes: int) -> void:
+	set_need_part("art", bytes)
+
+
+## The need in parts (the art; the surfaces a system's planets usually keep built
+## ahead): the room is twice their sum.
+static var _need_parts := {}
+static func set_need_part(part: String, bytes: int) -> void:
+	_need_parts[part] = bytes
+	need = 0
+	for k in _need_parts:
+		need += int(_need_parts[k])
+	budget = 2 * need
+
+
+## An asset is in: counted, used once. Over budget, the pool makes room.
+static func add(key: String, bytes: int, unload: Callable, held := Callable(), pinned := false, label := "") -> void:
+	var e: Entry = _e.get(key)
+	if e:
+		used += bytes - e.bytes
+		e.bytes = bytes
+	else:
+		e = Entry.new()
+		e.key = key
+		e.bytes = bytes
+		_e[key] = e
+		used += bytes
+	e.label = label if label != "" else key
+	e.unload = unload
+	e.held = held
+	e.pinned = pinned
+	loads += 1
+	peak = maxi(peak, used)
+	touch(key)
+	note("Loaded %s  (%s)" % [e.label, mb(bytes)], "load")
+	if budget > 0 and used > budget:
+		trim()
+
+
+## An asset used (drawn, handed out): its priority goes up by one.
+static func touch(key: String) -> void:
+	var e: Entry = _e.get(key)
+	if e:
+		var t := _now()
+		e.uses = e.uses * pow(0.5, (t - e.at) / HALF_LIFE) + 1.0
+		e.at = t
+
+
+## How much it's used (fading with time): the higher, the later it's unloaded.
+static func priority(key: String) -> float:
+	var e: Entry = _e.get(key)
+	if e == null:
+		return 0.0
+	return e.uses * pow(0.5, (_now() - e.at) / HALF_LIFE)
+
+
+static func has(key: String) -> bool:
+	return _e.has(key)
+
+
+## Its owner dropped it (no unload: the art reloaded, say).
+static func forget(key: String) -> void:
+	var e: Entry = _e.get(key)
+	if e:
+		used -= e.bytes
+		_e.erase(key)
+
+
+## Over budget: the least used assets nobody holds unloaded, until it fits.
+static func trim() -> void:
+	if used <= budget:
+		return
+	var free: Array = []
+	for e: Entry in _e.values():
+		if e.pinned or (e.held.is_valid() and e.held.call()):
+			continue
+		free.append([priority(e.key), e])
+	free.sort_custom(func(a, b): return a[0] < b[0])
+	for f in free:
+		if used <= budget:
+			break
+		var e: Entry = f[1]
+		_e.erase(e.key)
+		used -= e.bytes
+		unloads += 1
+		unloaded_bytes += e.bytes
+		if e.unload.is_valid():
+			e.unload.call()
+		note("Unloaded %s  (%s, priority %.1f) - the pool was full" % [e.label, mb(e.bytes), f[0]], "unload")
+	if used > budget:
+		note("Pool over budget: everything left is in use (%s / %s)" % [mb(used), mb(budget)], "unload")
+
+
+## A line in the loading console.
+static func note(text: String, kind := "work") -> void:
+	events.append([_now(), text, kind])
+	if events.size() > KEEP_EVENTS:
+		events.pop_front()
+	serial += 1
+
+
+static func count() -> int:
+	return _e.size()
+
+
+## "212.4 MB".
+static func mb(bytes: int) -> String:
+	return "%.1f MB" % (bytes / 1048576.0)
+
+
+## The pool's state in a line: "Memory pool 212.4 / 488.8 MB - 1093 assets - 0 unloaded".
+static func summary() -> String:
+	var s := "Memory pool %s / %s  -  %d assets" % [mb(used), mb(budget), _e.size()]
+	s += "  -  %d unloaded (%s)" % [unloads, mb(unloaded_bytes)] if unloads > 0 else "  -  none unloaded"
+	return s
+
+
+## The kinds of asset, for the memory map: [key prefix, name, colour] (the first match).
+const KINDS := [
+	["surface:", "Planet surfaces built ahead", Color(0.95, 0.55, 0.25)],
+	["placeholders", "Procedural placeholders (shown till each picture loads)", Color(0.4, 0.85, 0.55)],
+	["anatomy_", "Anatomy pictures (the Repair Bay)", Color(0.9, 0.35, 0.45)],
+	["image:", "Picture data (CPU copies for building textures)", Color(0.6, 0.6, 0.7)],
+	["monster_", "Monsters", Color(0.85, 0.3, 0.75)],
+	["creature_", "Creatures", Color(0.65, 0.4, 0.95)],
+	["tile_", "Buildings and ground tiles", Color(0.95, 0.8, 0.35)],
+	["ship_", "Ships", Color(0.3, 0.75, 1.0)],
+	["station_", "Stations", Color(0.3, 0.95, 0.75)],
+	["sky_", "Skies", Color(0.45, 0.6, 1.0)],
+	["fx_", "Effects", Color(1.0, 0.45, 0.3)],
+	["gate_", "Jump gates", Color(0.55, 0.95, 1.0)],
+	["npc_", "Citizens", Color(0.8, 0.95, 0.5)],
+	["", "Other", Color(0.75, 0.75, 0.75)],
+]
+
+
+static func kind_of(key: String) -> int:
+	for i in KINDS.size():
+		if key.begins_with(KINDS[i][0]):
+			return i
+	return KINDS.size() - 1
+
+
+## What's in the pool by kind: [{kind, name, color, bytes, count, top: [[label, bytes, priority]...]}],
+## biggest kind first; `top` its `top_n` biggest assets.
+static func breakdown(top_n := 8) -> Array:
+	var by := {}
+	for e: Entry in _e.values():
+		var k := kind_of(e.key)
+		if not by.has(k):
+			by[k] = {"kind": k, "name": KINDS[k][1], "color": KINDS[k][2], "bytes": 0, "count": 0, "items": []}
+		var d: Dictionary = by[k]
+		d["bytes"] += e.bytes
+		d["count"] += 1
+		d["items"].append([e.label, e.bytes, priority(e.key)])
+	var out := by.values()
+	for d in out:
+		var items: Array = d["items"]
+		items.sort_custom(func(a, b): return a[1] > b[1])
+		d["top"] = items.slice(0, top_n)
+		d.erase("items")
+	out.sort_custom(func(a, b): return a["bytes"] > b["bytes"])
+	return out
+
+
+## Back to empty (tests).
+static func reset() -> void:
+	_e.clear()
+	used = 0
+	peak = 0
+	loads = 0
+	unloads = 0
+	unloaded_bytes = 0
+	events.clear()
+	serial = 0
hunks.title: The memory pool
hunks.note: Assets register with their size, an unload callback, a held check and an optional pin. Every use raises the asset's priority. When the pool goes over budget, trim() frees the lowest-priority assets that are not held and not pinned, and logs each one. The pool also keeps a capped event log and a per-kind breakdown for the loading console.

bubbles.text: The priority decays exponentially: the old count is halved for every 300 s since the last use, then one is added. What you use now outranks what you used long ago.
Pinned assets (the anatomy pictures, the placeholders) and assets still referenced elsewhere, such as a texture on screen, are never candidates for unloading.
The candidates are sorted by priority, least used first, and unloaded one by one until the pool fits its budget again.
The room is twice the sum of the need parts: the art, plus the current system's planet surfaces built ahead.

files.explanation: BgWork sizes the worker pool. It now also paces background work on the main thread, such as planet surfaces built ahead, by time rather than by frames. That work gets 6% of each second, never more than 2 ms in one frame.

hunks.diff:
@@ -17,3 +17,25 @@ static func threads
 				cores = maxi(1, int(a.trim_prefix("--cores=")))
 		_n = maxi(1, cores / 4)
 	return _n
+
+
+## The main thread's time for background work (a planet's surface built ahead
+## while you fly): paced by time, not by frames - RATE of every second (at 600
+## FPS ~0.1 ms a frame, at 60 FPS ~1 ms), never more than CAP_US in one frame.
+## A fixed slice a frame (1 ms) took a 600 FPS frame from 1.1 to 2.3 ms; now it
+## takes about a sixteenth of the main thread whatever the frame rate.
+const RATE := 0.06
+const CAP_US := 2000.0
+static var _bank := 0.0
+static var _at := -1
+
+
+## This frame's share, taken (0 if the bank's empty): spend it, then yield.
+static func take() -> int:
+	var now := Time.get_ticks_usec()
+	if _at >= 0:
+		_bank = minf(CAP_US, _bank + (now - _at) * RATE)
+	_at = now
+	var us := int(_bank)
+	_bank -= us
+	return us
hunks.title: Main-thread time paced by the clock
hunks.note: take() adds 6% of the time since its last call to a bank, capped at 2 ms, and hands out the whole microseconds in it. At 600 FPS that is about 0.1 ms a frame; at 60 FPS about 1 ms. The fixed 1 ms slice it replaces had taken a 600 FPS frame from 1.1 to 2.3 ms.

bubbles.text: The time that passed times RATE goes into the bank. The cap keeps one long frame from building up a long burst of work afterwards.
The caller gets this frame's whole microseconds and keeps the fraction in the bank. It spends them, then yields until the next frame.

hunks.title: LoadBar, MemMap and Lines
hunks.note: LoadBar is a panel with the history, the pool's line, the arrow and progress bar, and the memory map. Four times a second it picks what to report: the system streaming in, then a planet built ahead or being landed on, then the ground near you, then the pictures, otherwise "All loaded". It redraws only when that changes. MemMap draws the pool as a strip coloured by asset kind, with a tooltip per area. Lines draws only the visible rows of a history of up to 1000 lines; the label it replaces laid out its whole text every second and caused 45 ms frames.

bubbles.text: AssetPool.serial counts every note. The console takes only the new ones since it last looked, so the history survives scene changes and nothing is copied twice.
The bar and the pool line are redrawn only when what they show changes. That keeps per-frame cost near zero at 600 FPS.

bubbles.at: var w: float = size.x * float(d["bytes"]) / room
bubbles.text: Each kind's width on the memory map is its share of the pool's room. Whatever is left at the right is free room, drawn dark.
Only the rows in view are drawn, starting at the scroll bar's value. The cost is the same with 10 lines or 1000.

hunks.title: The background warm-up
hunks.note: Runs the same 60 trade rounds and price notes as before, but yields to the next frame whenever 1.5 ms are used, and stops if another game replaced the stations meanwhile.

A time budget per frame (1.5 ms), not a count of rounds, so the cost stays the same whatever the frame rate.

files.explanation: New file. HealthGauge replaces the shield and hull bars in the space HUD, and the automaton's health and shield on a planet. It shows the ship's (or automaton's) outline filled with red liquid as high as the hull is, inside a 150 px ring filled with blue liquid as high as the shields are. The affliction badges sit round the ring, clockwise from the top, and the numbers are written underneath.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,150 @@ 
+class_name HealthGauge
+extends Control
+## The health gauge (the space HUD's, and on foot the surface HUD's): the
+## outline of your ship (or of the automaton) filled with red liquid as high as
+## its hull (health) is - a wavy, moving surface (shaders/gauge_fill) - inside a
+## blue ring filled the same way as high as its shields are (gauge_ring); round
+## the circle, clockwise from the top, an icon for each affliction (a damaged
+## part: AfflictionBar's badges, their tooltips); under it the numbers.
+##   var g := HealthGauge.new(); g.which = "ship"; g.read = func(): return [hull, max_hull, shields, max_shields]
+##   g.silhouette = ship's texture; g.condition = func(): return data.condition
+
+const RING := 150.0           # the ring's diameter (px)
+const ICON_GAP := 6.0
+const STEP_DEG := 30.0        # between two affliction icons, clockwise from the top
+const FILL := preload("res://shaders/gauge_fill.gdshader")
+const RING_SHADER := preload("res://shaders/gauge_ring.gdshader")
+
+var which := "ship"
+## [hull, max hull, shields, max shields] - read a few times a second.
+var read: Callable
+## The parts' condition (Parts.afflictions) - for the icons round the circle.
+var condition: Callable
+## The outline's picture, looked at a few times a second (a new ship: its outline).
+var shape_source: Callable
+var hull_name := "HULL"
+var shield_name := "SHIELDS"
+var silhouette: Texture2D:
+	set(t):
+		silhouette = t
+		if _shape:
+			_shape.texture = t
+			_fit_shape()
+
+var _ring: ColorRect
+var _shape: TextureRect
+var _icons: Control
+var _vals := [1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0]
+var _shown := [-1.0, -1.0]
+var _sig := "-"
+var _t := 0.0
+
+
+func _ready() -> void:
+	var side := RING + 2.0 * (AfflictionBar.ICON + ICON_GAP)
+	custom_minimum_size = Vector2(side, side + 20.0)
+	mouse_filter = MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE
+	_ring = ColorRect.new()
+	_ring.size = Vector2(RING, RING)
+	_ring.position = Vector2((side - RING) / 2.0, (side - RING) / 2.0)
+	_ring.mouse_filter = MOUSE_FILTER_STOP
+	_ring.tooltip_text = "Shields (the blue ring) and hull (the red inside)"
+	var rm := ShaderMaterial.new()
+	rm.shader = RING_SHADER
+	_ring.material = rm
+	add_child(_ring)
+	_shape = TextureRect.new()
+	_shape.expand_mode = TextureRect.EXPAND_IGNORE_SIZE
+	_shape.stretch_mode = TextureRect.STRETCH_KEEP_ASPECT_CENTERED
+	_shape.mouse_filter = MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE
+	var fm := ShaderMaterial.new()
+	fm.shader = FILL
+	fm.set_shader_parameter("seed", randf() * 10.0)
+	_shape.material = fm
+	_shape.texture = silhouette
+	add_child(_shape)
+	_fit_shape()
+	_icons = Control.new()
+	_icons.mouse_filter = MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE
+	add_child(_icons)
+	_refresh()
+
+
+func _fit_shape() -> void:
+	if _shape == null or _ring == null:
+		return
+	var inner := RING * 0.74
+	_shape.size = Vector2(inner, inner)
+	_shape.position = _ring.position + Vector2(RING - inner, RING - inner) / 2.0
+	if silhouette:
+		var s := silhouette.get_size()
+		(_shape.material as ShaderMaterial).set_shader_parameter("px", Vector2(2.5, 2.5) / (inner * Vector2(1.0, s.y / maxf(1.0, s.x)).max(Vector2.ONE)))
+
+
+func _process(delta: float) -> void:
+	_t -= delta
+	if _t > 0.0:
+		return
+	_t = 0.1
+	_refresh()
+
+
+## Looked at again now (the icons too).
+func refresh() -> void:
+	_sig = "-"
+	_refresh()
+
+
+## The affliction icons round the circle (in clockwise order).
+func icons() -> Array:
+	return _icons.get_children().filter(func(c): return not c.is_queued_for_deletion())
+
+
+func _refresh() -> void:
+	if shape_source.is_valid():
+		var t = shape_source.call()
+		if t is Texture2D and t != silhouette:
+			silhouette = t
+	if read.is_valid():
+		_vals = read.call()
+	var hk := clampf(float(_vals[0]) / maxf(1.0, float(_vals[1])), 0.0, 1.0)
+	var sk := clampf(float(_vals[2]) / maxf(1.0, float(_vals[3])), 0.0, 1.0) if float(_vals[3]) > 0.0 else 0.0
+	if hk != _shown[0] or sk != _shown[1]:
+		_shown = [hk, sk]
+		(_shape.material as ShaderMaterial).set_shader_parameter("level", hk)
+		(_ring.material as ShaderMaterial).set_shader_parameter("level", sk)
+		queue_redraw()
+	_refresh_icons()
+
+
+## The afflictions round the circle, clockwise from the top (rebuilt only when they change).
+func _refresh_icons() -> void:
+	var cond = condition.call() if condition.is_valid() else null
+	var list: Array = Parts.afflictions(cond, which) if cond is Dictionary else []
+	var sig := ",".join(list.map(func(a): return "%s:%d" % [a["id"], roundi(float(a["loss"]) * 20.0)]))
+	if sig == _sig:
+		return
+	_sig = sig
+	for c in _icons.get_children():
+		c.queue_free()
+	var centre := _ring.position + Vector2(RING, RING) / 2.0
+	var r := RING / 2.0 + ICON_GAP + AfflictionBar.ICON / 2.0
+	for i in list.size():
+		var ang := deg_to_rad(-90.0 + i * STEP_DEG)
+		var ic := AfflictionBar.icon_for(list[i], which)
+		ic.position = centre + Vector2.from_angle(ang) * r - Vector2(AfflictionBar.ICON, AfflictionBar.ICON) / 2.0
+		_icons.add_child(ic)
+
+
+## The numbers under the circle: hull (red), shields (blue).
+func _draw() -> void:
+	var font := get_theme_default_font()
+	var y := custom_minimum_size.y - 5.0
+	var w := size.x
+	var hull_t := "%s %d" % [hull_name, ceili(float(_vals[0]))]
+	var sh_t := "%s %d" % [shield_name, ceili(float(_vals[2]))]
+	var tw := font.get_string_size(hull_t, HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_LEFT, -1, 14).x
+	var sw := font.get_string_size(sh_t, HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_LEFT, -1, 14).x
+	var x0 := (w - tw - sw - 24.0) / 2.0
+	draw_string(font, Vector2(x0, y), hull_t, HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_LEFT, -1, 14, Color(1.0, 0.45, 0.4))
+	draw_string(font, Vector2(x0 + tw + 24.0, y), sh_t, HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_LEFT, -1, 14, Color(0.5, 0.78, 1.0))
hunks.title: The health gauge control
hunks.note: A ColorRect drawn with the ring shader and a TextureRect of the silhouette drawn with the fill shader. Ten times a second it reads [hull, max hull, shields, max shields] through a callable and passes the shares to the shaders as `level`. It rebuilds the affliction icons only when the list of afflictions changes.

bubbles.text: The shader animates the hull's share as the liquid's height. Script only touches it when the value changes.
Affliction icons go round the circle from the top (-90 degrees), 30 degrees apart, clockwise. They are placed just outside the ring.
A signature of each affliction's id and rounded loss. The icons are only freed and rebuilt when it changes.
The outline follows the current sprite. A new ship, or a placeholder replaced by its real picture, gives a new silhouette.

files.explanation: main.gd is the space scene: it builds the current solar system and runs flight, landing and saving. In this patch a system no longer appears all at once behind a hidden scene: only the core (ship, HUD, panels) is made before you fly, and every planet, moon, station, gate, nebula, ship, monster and asteroid field becomes a queued piece made nearest to the ship first, a few per frame within 2.5 ms, each fading in. The scene also builds every landable planet's surface ahead in the background, one at a time, keeps them in the memory pool and parks finished ones out of the tree, so landing plays only the animation. Measured: a new game's still time went from 595 ms to about 150 ms before you fly.

hunks.title: The piece queue
hunks.note: The staged build now yields only when a 3 ms frame share is used, and a new piece queue streams the system in by distance. Pieces made during the staged start are held hidden and still, then revealed a few a frame while the scene already runs; the Ship Computer is prewarmed only after every piece is in.

bubbles.at: func _piece(key: String, what: String, at: Vector2, run: Callable, needs := Callable()) -> void:
bubbles.text: Each piece is a key, a label for the loading console, a place, the work to run and an optional condition. Built directly (tests) the work runs at once; streaming, it is queued.

bubbles.at: while not _pieces.is_empty() and Time.get_ticks_usec() - t0 < PIECES_US:
bubbles.text: Each frame the pump picks the nearest ready piece to the ship (skipping ones whose `needs` is not met yet, like a moon before its planet) and makes it, until 2.5 ms are spent.
While a piece is made, node_added collects the new top-level visuals; each starts transparent and fades in over 0.4 s so nothing pops.
The scene stays visible during the staged start (no black screen): instead, each world piece added is hidden and its processing disabled until _stage_end reveals it.

 var _landing_surface: Node = null
 
+
+## Every landable planet's surface built ahead, hidden, from the moment you're
+## in a system - one at a time, the nearest not built yet first - and kept:
+## landing on any of them takes the animation only. Each built one is in the
+## memory pool (AssetPool "surface:<id>": used more while you're near it),
+## unloaded only if the pool runs out of room, the least used first. They go
+## with this scene (a jump, a landing: the others taken apart a few ms a frame).
+const PREBUILD_R := 4000.0
+## (its size in memory, measured 2026-11-20: five surfaces 199 MB of memory and
+## 14 MB of textures - its arrays, ~2400 nodes, tile layers, ground pictures, map)
+const SURFACE_BYTES := 44 * 1048576
+## How many a browser keeps built ahead (a tab has far less memory: the nearest few).
+const WEB_SURFACES := 3
+var _surfaces := {}          # planet id -> its surface (built, or being built)
+var _prebuilt: Node = null   # the one being built now (the loading console)
+var _prebuilt_id := ""
+var _prebuild_t := 1.5   # (not in the system's first moments)
+## (off in headless runs - the tests, but the one that checks it)
+var prebuild_on := DisplayServer.get_name() != "headless"
+
+
+## A surface built (or being built) ahead for `pid` - null if none.
+func surface_ahead(pid: String) -> Node:
+	var s: Node = _surfaces.get(pid)
+	return s if is_instance_valid(s) else null
+
+
+func _prebuild_tick(delta: float) -> void:
+	_prebuild_t -= delta
+	if _prebuild_t > 0.0:
+		return
+	_prebuild_t = 0.5
+	if not prebuild_on or SaveGame.travelling or is_instance_valid(_landing_surface) or not ship.is_alive():
+		return
+	# The nearest planet's surface used: it stays longest in the pool.
+	var near: Node2D = null
+	var near_d := INF
+	var next: Node2D = null
+	var next_d := INF
+	for b in get_tree().get_nodes_in_group("planet_bodies"):
+		if b.landable and b.planet_id != "":
+			var d: float = b.global_position.distance_to(ship.global_position)
+			if d < near_d:
+				near_d = d
+				near = b
+			if surface_ahead(b.planet_id) == null and d < next_d:
+				next_d = d
+				next = b
+	# (the pool's usual need: this system's surfaces too - its room twice that)
+	var landable := get_tree().get_nodes_in_group("planet_bodies").filter(func(b): return b.landable and b.planet_id != "").size()
+	if OS.has_feature("web"):
+		landable = mini(landable, WEB_SURFACES)
+		if _surfaces.size() >= WEB_SURFACES:
+			next = null   # (a browser: the nearest few only)
+	AssetPool.set_need_part("surfaces", landable * SURFACE_BYTES)
+	if near and near_d < PREBUILD_R:
+		AssetPool.touch("surface:" + near.planet_id)
+	if is_instance_valid(_prebuilt):
+		if not _prebuilt.is_built:
+			return   # (one at a time)
+		var pid := _prebuilt_id
+		_prebuilt = null
+		_prebuilt_id = ""
+		AssetPool.add("surface:" + pid, SURFACE_BYTES, _drop_surface.bind(pid), Callable(), false,
+			"Surface of " + str(Planets.get_planet(pid).get("name", pid)))
+	# A built one whose streaming has settled waits out of the tree (parked): in
+	# it, its ~2400 hidden, stopped nodes still cost the frame (~11%, measured);
+	# out of it, nothing. One a tick (~11 ms); put back as you land (~9 ms).
+	for pid in _surfaces:
+		var sf: Node = _surfaces[pid]
+		if is_instance_valid(sf) and sf != _prebuilt and sf.is_built and sf.is_inside_tree() and sf.streaming_idle():
+			sf.get_parent().remove_child(sf)
+			break
+	if next != null:
+		_prebuild(next.planet_id)
+
+
+func _prebuild(pid: String) -> void:
+	var surface: Node = load(SURFACE_SCENE).instantiate()
+	surface.prebuilding = true
+	surface.background = true
+	surface.planet_override = pid
+	surface.state_override = get_save_data()
+	get_tree().root.add_child(surface)
+	_surfaces[pid] = surface
+	_prebuilt = surface
+	_prebuilt_id = pid
+	AssetPool.note("Building the surface of %s ahead (%d of %d)" % [str(Planets.get_planet(pid).get("name", pid)), _surfaces.size(),
+		get_tree().get_nodes_in_group("planet_bodies").filter(func(b): return b.landable and b.planet_id != "").size()])
+
+
+## A surface built ahead let go (the pool ran out of room, or this scene goes).
+func _drop_surface(pid: String) -> void:
+	var s: Node = _surfaces.get(pid)
+	_surfaces.erase(pid)
+	AssetPool.forget("surface:" + pid)
+	if s == _prebuilt:
+		_prebuilt = null
+		_prebuilt_id = ""
+	if is_instance_valid(s):
+		if not s.is_inside_tree():
+			s.queue_free()   # (parked out of the tree: freed without the tree's notifications)
+		elif s.is_built:
+			s.discard = true   # (its ground streaming stops at once: nothing made into what's being taken apart)
+			UI.dismantle(s)   # (a few ms a frame)
+		else:
+			s.discard = true   # (still being built: it finishes, quietly, then takes itself apart - freed at once was a 340 ms frame)
+
+
+func _drop_prebuild() -> void:
+	for pid in _surfaces.keys():
+		_drop_surface(pid)

hunks.title: Landing on a surface built ahead; the pre-builder
hunks.note: Landing takes a surface already built ahead (putting it back in the tree if parked, then giving it the current game state), else builds one as before. The new pre-builder builds every landable planet's surface one at a time, nearest first, registers each in the memory pool at 44 MB, and parks settled ones out of the tree, which measured about 11% of the frame when kept in.

bubbles.text: A surface built earlier gets the game as it is now (credits, gear, ship picture), since it was built from an older snapshot.

bubbles.at: if surface_ahead(b.planet_id) == null and d < next_d:
bubbles.text: Twice a second the tick finds the nearest landable planet with no surface yet; that is the next one built (a browser keeps only the nearest three).
Parking: a finished surface whose ground streaming has settled is taken out of the tree, one per tick, so its ~2400 hidden nodes cost nothing per frame.

bubbles.at: s.discard = true   # (still being built: it finishes, quietly, then takes itself apart - freed at once was a 340 ms frame)
bubbles.text: Dropping a surface depends on its state: parked ones are freed directly, built ones are dismantled a few ms a frame, and one still building is flagged to take itself apart when it finishes.

files.explanation: New file. PlaceholderArt makes a procedural placeholder for each sprite: a simple, low-detail shape for its kind (a hull with swept wings, a station ring, a beast, a robed figure, an isometric block, a ring, a diamond, a glow, a sky band or a slab), in the sprite's two main colours and fitted to its opaque box. ProcArt shows these first, and each real picture replaces its placeholder when it loads.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,113 @@ 
+class_name PlaceholderArt
+extends RefCounted
+## Procedural placeholders: what a sprite looks like before its picture is
+## loaded - a simple, low-detail shape for its kind (a ship's hull, a station's
+## ring, a beast, a building's block, a figure, a glow...) in the sprite's own
+## two main colours, fitted to where its picture is opaque (data/sprites/
+## sizes.json: tools/sprite_sizes.py). Made in microseconds (each kind's shape a
+## 48 px mask drawn once; a placeholder is two masked blits), so every sprite
+## has one long before the pictures load: ProcArt draws them all first, then
+## loads the real pictures, each replacing its placeholder in place.
+
+const RES := 48
+
+## [key prefix, kind]: the first that matches.
+const KINDS := [
+	["ship_", "hull"], ["station_", "station"], ["monster_", "beast"], ["creature_", "beast"],
+	["npc_", "figure"], ["tile_", "block"], ["gate_", "ring"], ["minimap_", "ring"],
+	["nav_", "diamond"], ["fx_", "glow"], ["sky_", "band"],
+]
+
+static var _masks := {}   # kind -> [base, top] (Images, RES x RES, alpha the shape)
+
+
+static func kind_of(key: String) -> String:
+	for k in KINDS:
+		if key.begins_with(k[0]):
+			return k[1]
+	return "slab"
+
+
+## The placeholder's picture (RES x RES; drawn at the sprite's size). `meta`:
+## sizes.json's [w, h, main, shade, x0, y0, x1, y1].
+static func make(key: String, meta: Array) -> Image:
+	var m: Array = _mask(kind_of(key))
+	var x0 := int(RES * float(meta[4]) / 100.0) if meta.size() > 7 else 0
+	var y0 := int(RES * float(meta[5]) / 100.0) if meta.size() > 7 else 0
+	var x1 := int(ceil(RES * float(meta[6]) / 100.0)) if meta.size() > 7 else RES
+	var y1 := int(ceil(RES * float(meta[7]) / 100.0)) if meta.size() > 7 else RES
+	var bw := clampi(x1 - x0, 2, RES)
+	var bh := clampi(y1 - y0, 2, RES)
+	var main := Color.html(str(meta[2])) if meta.size() > 2 else Color(0.6, 0.7, 0.8)
+	var shade := Color.html(str(meta[3])) if meta.size() > 3 else main.darkened(0.35)
+	var img := Image.create(RES, RES, false, Image.FORMAT_RGBA8)
+	for layer in 2:
+		var mask: Image = m[layer]
+		if bw != RES or bh != RES:
+			mask = mask.duplicate()
+			mask.resize(bw, bh, Image.INTERPOLATE_NEAREST)
+		var col: Color = shade if layer == 0 else main.lightened(0.12)
+		col.a = 0.95
+		var solid := Image.create(bw, bh, false, Image.FORMAT_RGBA8)
+		solid.fill(col)
+		img.blit_rect_mask(solid, mask, Rect2i(0, 0, bw, bh), Vector2i(x0, y0))
+	return img
+
+
+## A kind's two masks (its whole shape; its lit top), drawn once.
+static func _mask(kind: String) -> Array:
+	if _masks.has(kind):
+		return _masks[kind]
+	var out := []
+	for layer in 2:
+		var img := Image.create(RES, RES, false, Image.FORMAT_RGBA8)
+		for y in RES:
+			for x in RES:
+				if _inside(kind, layer, (x + 0.5) / RES, (y + 0.5) / RES):
+					img.set_pixel(x, y, Color(1, 1, 1, 1))
+		out.append(img)
+	_masks[kind] = out
+	return out
+
+
+## Is (u, v) (0..1 across the sprite) in the shape - its whole (layer 0) or its lit top (1)?
+static func _inside(kind: String, layer: int, u: float, v: float) -> bool:
+	var p := Vector2(u, v)
+	match kind:
+		"hull":   # (a pointed hull with swept wings, nose up)
+			var body := absf(u - 0.5) < 0.24 * (1.0 - absf(v - 0.55) / 0.55) + 0.05 and v > 0.03 and v < 0.97
+			var wings := v > 0.35 and v < 0.85 and absf(u - 0.5) < (v - 0.35) * 0.95
+			return (body or wings) if layer == 0 else (absf(u - 0.5) < 0.07 and v > 0.12 and v < 0.75)
+		"station":   # (a ring on spokes round a core)
+			var d := p.distance_to(Vector2(0.5, 0.5))
+			if layer == 1:
+				return d < 0.15
+			return (d > 0.3 and d < 0.47) or d < 0.17 or (d < 0.47 and (absf(u - 0.5) < 0.04 or absf(v - 0.5) < 0.04))
+		"beast":   # (a body, a head, legs)
+			var body := pow((u - 0.47) / 0.36, 2) + pow((v - 0.55) / 0.24, 2) < 1.0
+			var head := p.distance_to(Vector2(0.8, 0.35)) < 0.15
+			var legs := v > 0.6 and v < 0.97 and (absf(u - 0.27) < 0.05 or absf(u - 0.42) < 0.05 or absf(u - 0.58) < 0.05 or absf(u - 0.7) < 0.05)
+			if layer == 1:
+				return pow((u - 0.45) / 0.28, 2) + pow((v - 0.45) / 0.12, 2) < 1.0 or p.distance_to(Vector2(0.8, 0.33)) < 0.09
+			return body or head or legs
+		"figure":   # (a head on a robed body)
+			var head := p.distance_to(Vector2(0.5, 0.15)) < 0.12
+			var robe := v > 0.28 and v < 0.98 and absf(u - 0.5) < 0.16 + (v - 0.28) * 0.18
+			return (head or robe) if layer == 0 else head
+		"block":   # (an isometric block: a lit top, two walls)
+			var top := absf(u - 0.5) / 0.5 + absf(v - 0.27) / 0.25 < 1.0
+			var walls := v > 0.27 and v < 0.75 + 0.25 * (1.0 - absf(u - 0.5) / 0.5) and u > 0.0 and u < 1.0
+			return (top or walls) if layer == 0 else top
+		"ring":
+			var d := p.distance_to(Vector2(0.5, 0.5))
+			return (d > 0.32 and d < 0.48) if layer == 0 else (d > 0.39 and d < 0.43)
+		"diamond":
+			var k := absf(u - 0.5) + absf(v - 0.5)
+			return k < 0.48 if layer == 0 else k < 0.2
+		"glow":
+			var d := p.distance_to(Vector2(0.5, 0.5))
+			return d < 0.45 if layer == 0 else d < 0.2
+		"band":
+			return true if layer == 0 else v < 0.35
+	# (anything else: a slab with a lit top edge)
+	return (u > 0.06 and u < 0.94 and v > 0.06 and v < 0.94) if layer == 0 else (u > 0.06 and u < 0.94 and v > 0.06 and v < 0.3)
hunks.title: Procedural placeholder shapes
hunks.note: Each kind's shape is drawn once as two 48 px masks, the whole shape and its lit top. After that, a placeholder is just two masked blits of solid colour into a 48 px image, made by the engine with no pixel loops in script. The colours and the opaque box come from sizes.json, which tools/sprite_sizes.py writes.

bubbles.text: The sprite's key prefix picks the shape (KINDS). Anything unmatched becomes a slab with a lit top edge.

bubbles.at: img.blit_rect_mask(solid, mask, Rect2i(0, 0, bw, bh), Vector2i(x0, y0))
bubbles.text: The two layers are blitted through the cached mask, scaled to the sprite's opaque box. The shade colour goes underneath, then the lightened main colour on top.
The only per-pixel loop. It runs once per kind (48 x 48 tests) and is cached in _masks, so all 1093 placeholders reuse about a dozen masks.

bubbles.at: static func _inside(kind: String, layer: int, u: float, v: float) -> bool:
bubbles.text: Each shape is a small implicit test in 0..1 coordinates: distances for rings and glows, ellipses for beasts, and lines for hulls and blocks.

+func _gen_index(c: Vector2i) -> int:
+	return clampi(c.x / GEN, 0, GEN_N - 1) * GEN_N + clampi(c.y / GEN, 0, GEN_N - 1)

+func gen_ready(c: Vector2i) -> bool:

+		return false

+## Every chunk under `r` in.
+func gen_ready_rect(r: Rect2i) -> bool:
+	if not _streamed:
+		return true
+	var a := r.intersection(Rect2i(0, 0, N, N))
+	for x in range(a.position.x / GEN, (a.end.x - 1) / GEN + 1):
+		for y in range(a.position.y / GEN, (a.end.y - 1) / GEN + 1):
+			if _gen_done[x * GEN_N + y] == 0:

+func streaming_idle() -> bool:

+		and _chunk_tasks.is_empty() and _place_queue.is_empty()

+## The ground round you: [chunks in, of all within reach (STREAM_R)] - the loading console's bar.

+	var out := Vector2i.ZERO
+	for idx in GEN_N * GEN_N:
+		if Vector2(idx / GEN_N + 0.5, idx % GEN_N + 0.5).distance_squared_to(hc) < STREAM_R * STREAM_R:
+			out.y += 1

+## Each frame: the worker's next job started (the nearest chunk not made), what
+## it made taken in - within a few ms.
+func _pump_gen() -> void:

+	if _gen_task < 0 and _planned and _take_q.size() < 2 and (not background or Time.get_ticks_msec() - _gen_at >= BG_GEN_GAP_MS):

+		if next >= 0:
+			_gen_busy[next] = true
+			var cx := next / GEN_N
+			var cy := next % GEN_N
+			_gen_task = WorkerThreadPool.add_task(func(): _gen_result = _planner.chunk(cx, cy), false, "Planet chunk")

+	if not _take_q.is_empty():
+		budget = BgWork.take() if background else (TAKE_BG_US if prebuilding else TAKE_US)   # (built ahead: the paced share)

+		if _take_step(_take_q[0]):

+var _want_areas: Array = []

+## Waits until every chunk under `area` (cells) is in - made first.
+func stream_area(area: Rect2i) -> void:

+	_want_areas.append(a)

+## Where you were when nothing near was left to make (the search skipped till you move).
+var _idle_at := Vector2i(-1, -1)

+func _next_chunk() -> int:
+	for a in _want_areas:
+		var hc0 := Vector2(a.get_center()) / GEN
+		var best0 := -1
+		var bd := INF
+		for x in range(a.position.x / GEN, (a.end.x - 1) / GEN + 1):
+			for y in range(a.position.y / GEN, (a.end.y - 1) / GEN + 1):
+				var idx := x * GEN_N + y
+				if _gen_done[idx] == 1 or _gen_busy.has(idx):
+					continue
+				var d := Vector2(x + 0.5, y + 0.5).distance_squared_to(hc0)
+				if d < bd:
+					bd = d
+					best0 = idx
+		if best0 >= 0:
+			return best0
+	var here := _cell_at(pilot.position) if pilot else Vector2i(N / 2, N / 2)
+	var hc := Vector2(here) / GEN
+	var at := Vector2i(hc * 4.0)   # (a quarter chunk: no new search until you've moved that far)
+	if _want_areas.is_empty() and at == _idle_at:
+		return -1   # (all round you's in: nothing to look for each frame)
+	var best := -1
+	var best_d := STREAM_R * STREAM_R   # (only what's near you: the rest when you go there)
+	for idx in GEN_N * GEN_N:
+		if _gen_done[idx] == 1 or _gen_busy.has(idx):
+			continue
+		var d := Vector2(idx / GEN_N + 0.5, idx % GEN_N + 0.5).distance_squared_to(hc)
+		if d < best_d:
+			best_d = d

+		var tt: PackedByteArray = res["terrain"]
+		var rp: PackedFloat32Array = res["ramp"]
+		var ll: PackedByteArray = res["lvl"]
+		var rd: PackedByteArray = res["rampd"]
+		for a in r.size.x:
+			for b in r.size.y:

+		var box := Rect2(corners[0], Vector2.ZERO)
+		for c in corners:

hunks.title: Streaming the planet chunk by chunk
hunks.note: The heart of the change. A tiled planet without an editor layout is no longer made whole: a SurfacePlanner plans it on a worker, then makes 32 x 32 tile chunks nearest-first while _pump_gen takes each one in within a few ms a frame. A placeholder plate in the ground's colour covers what isn't made yet; the old whole-planet path survives as _build_whole for untiled or hand-laid planets.

bubbles.text: The new path: the surface opens as soon as the plan and the chunks under the pad's path-finding window are in; the rest streams while you play.
One worker job at a time: first setup and plan (plus the tile set and the predecoded scenery pictures), later one chunk per job. The job's output lands in _gen_result for the main thread.

Runs every frame from process_frame (so a hidden, still surface built ahead streams too): collects a finished job, starts the next nearest chunk, then spends up to 2.5 ms (1 ms or BgWork's paced share when built ahead) taking queued chunks in.

Takes one chunk in over several frames: first its arrays and map pixels are copied in, then its tiles are set 500 at a time; at the end it is marked ready, its ground pictures redrawn (GroundChunks.refresh) and its animals queued.

files.explanation: ProcArt is the game's sprite store. It used to load all 1093 sprites before the game could start. Now it loads them in the background for the whole game. First it makes a procedural placeholder for every sprite. Then it loads the real pictures a few at a time, within a time budget each frame, with the requested ones first. Each picture replaces its placeholder in place. It also loads the space, surface and station scenes behind the title screen. Every loaded picture is registered with the new memory pool (AssetPool), which can unload it if room runs out.

hunks.title: Streaming loader and placeholders first
hunks.note: _load_all no longer waits for every sprite. It reads sizes.json and sets the pool's budget from it. Then it makes a procedural placeholder for every sprite, 4 ms a frame, and hands the rest to _process. _process loads 8 sprites at once on a desktop (3 in a browser, which loads them on the main thread within 8 ms a frame). It takes finished pictures in within 3 ms a frame, with the requested ones first.

bubbles.at: if not placeholders_done or (_queue.is_empty() and _urgent.is_empty() and _flight.is_empty()):
bubbles.text: No real picture loads until every placeholder is drawn: the procedural placeholders get full priority.
Taking finished loads in creates their textures on the main thread. A 3 ms budget a frame spreads that work over several frames, so the frame rate holds.
The pool's budget is twice the usual need: the size of every sprite from sizes.json (w x h x 4 bytes) plus the anatomy pictures. That comes to about 547 MB on a desktop.
Placeholders are made in 4 ms slices with a yield to the next frame between them. All 1093 are ready in well under a second, and no frame stalls.

hunks.title: sprite(), get_tex(), prefetch and ensure
hunks.note: get_tex always returns the real picture. It is for code that reads pixels or bakes atlases. sprite() returns at once, giving the placeholder if the picture isn't in yet and putting it at the front of the queue. prefetch and ensure let a planet surface ask for its own tiles and creatures first and wait for them across frames, with no loading on the spot. When a picture arrives, _take copies it into the placeholder's texture, so whatever holds that texture now shows the real art.

bubbles.text: This is the drawing path. It never waits. A picture that isn't in, or that the pool has unloaded, comes back as a placeholder and is queued as urgent.
The placeholder's ImageTexture takes the real image, so its RID stays the same. Sprites and atlases that already hold it update with no rewiring. Reading the picture back costs about 0.15 ms.
A texture is held when something other than ProcArt references it, for example a sprite on screen. The pool never unloads a held texture.
Waits frame by frame until no sprite with the given prefixes is queued, in flight or still a placeholder. A surface uses this before it bakes its ground tiles.

files.explanation: New: the planet's maker split into units that run on a worker thread - setup (the planet's constants), plan (villages, gates, bands, industry, touching only the ground near them) and chunk (one 32 x 32 square: levels, ramps, links, tiles, map pixels, animals). Terrain is made lazily in 16 x 16 blocks and kept, and every unit seeds itself from the planet's seed, so the same planet comes out the same in any order. This is what lets the ground stream in round you instead of a multi-second whole-planet build.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,1094 @@ 
+class_name SurfacePlanner
+extends RefCounted
+## A tiled planet made a piece at a time (PlanetSurface streams it): nothing
+## is generated for the whole planet at once. On a worker thread, one job at a
+## time (the surface queues them):
+##   setup()        the planet's constants (noise, the water's shape, the height
+##                  scale and the site height from a coarse sample) - a moment
+##   plan()         where the villages, palaces, gates, pirate bands and
+##                  industrial sites go - looking only at the terrain near them
+##   chunk(cx, cy)  a GEN x GEN square: its ground (bands, ledges, plots
+##                  levelled, ramps natural and linking), its tiles, its map
+##                  pixels and its animals - returned as small arrays the
+##                  surface copies into its own (it never touches these)
+## The terrain is computed lazily in BLOCK x BLOCK blocks, on demand, and kept
+## (_raw): the plan's edits (levelled plots, slopes) are applied to it, so every
+## chunk sees them. The same planet (seed) always comes out the same, chunk by
+## chunk, in any order.
+
+const N := 440
+const BLOCK := 16
+const GEN := 32                     # a chunk (2 x the surface's scenery CHUNK)
+const NB := N / BLOCK + 1
+const REGION := 110
+const VILLAGE_CHANCE := 0.45
+const PIRATE_BANDS := 23
+const WILD_GATES := 6
+const GATE_APART := 45.0
+const GATE_NAMES := ["Alpha", "Beta", "Gamma", "Delta", "Epsilon", "Zeta", "Eta", "Theta", "Iota", "Kappa",
+	"Lambda", "Mu", "Nu", "Xi", "Omicron", "Pi", "Rho", "Sigma", "Tau", "Upsilon", "Phi", "Chi", "Psi", "Omega"]
+const PLOT_EASE := 10
+const INDUSTRY_SITES := 14
+const INDUSTRY_R := 4
+## Islands (sky platforms): walkways along a lattice, LATTICE tiles apart, BRIDGE wide.
+const LATTICE := 36
+const BRIDGE := 3
+const MAP_SEA := Color(0.014, 0.02, 0.032)
+const MAP_SHALLOW := Color(0.03, 0.045, 0.062)
+const MAP_LAND := Color(0.085, 0.06, 0.032)
+const MAP_LIT := Color(1.0, 0.56, 0.16)
+const MAP_COAST := Color(1.0, 0.76, 0.42)
+const MAP_GRID := 44
+const MAP_ELEV_HIGH := Color(0.88, 0.92, 0.8)
+const NB4 := [Vector2i(1, 0), Vector2i(-1, 0), Vector2i(0, 1), Vector2i(0, -1),
+	Vector2i(2, 0), Vector2i(-2, 0), Vector2i(0, 2), Vector2i(0, -2)]
+
+const TTILES := preload("res://scripts/terrain_tiles.gd")
+const BUILDINGS := ["warehouse", "temple"]
+
+# Given by the surface.
+var pdata: Dictionary
+var planet_id := ""
+var seed_ := 0
+var tile_set_id := ""
+var tile_pieces: Array = []
+var culture_name := "Minoan"
+var sky := false
+var g2w: Transform2D                 # grid -> world (the surface's _g2w)
+
+# The planet's constants (setup).
+var th := PackedFloat32Array()
+var walk_t := PackedByteArray()
+var water_top := -1.0
+var site_h := 0.0
+var plot_lvl := 0
+var lvl_top := 1
+var _wl := 0
+var _land_lo := -0.62
+var _water := ""
+var _lo := 0.0
+var _hi := 1.0
+var _ridge: FastNoiseLite
+var _hills: FastNoiseLite
+var _crag: FastNoiseLite
+var _bumps: FastNoiseLite
+var _wiggle: FastNoiseLite
+var _meander: FastNoiseLite
+var _rn: FastNoiseLite
+var _isle: FastNoiseLite
+var _n1: FastNoiseLite               # tile looks (TerrainTiles.ground_piece)
+var _n2: FastNoiseLite
+var _coast_dir := Vector2.RIGHT
+var _islets: Array = []
+var _lake := {}
+var _river := {}
+var _cen := Vector2(N / 2.0, N / 2.0)
+
+# The terrain, made lazily by block, with the plan's edits.
+var _height := PackedFloat32Array()
+var _ramp := PackedFloat32Array()
+var _terrain := PackedByteArray()
+var _block_done := PackedByteArray()
+
+# The plan (plan()).
+var plans: Array = []                # {spec, built: null}
+var npc_plans: Array = []
+var plot_cells := {}
+var clear_spots: Array = []          # [cell, radius]
+var village_spots: Array = []
+var gates: Array = []
+var industry: Array = []
+var village_fauna: Array = []        # fauna plans by the villages (the rest: a chunk's own)
+var atlas_looks: Array = []
+var tile_ts: TileSet
+var planned := false
+var _rng := RandomNumberGenerator.new()
+
+
+## (worker) The planet's constants; heavy-ish parts are coarse (1/8 sample).
+func setup() -> void:
+	th = PackedFloat32Array(pdata["thresholds"])
+	var terr: Array = pdata["terrain"]
+	walk_t = PackedByteArray()
+	for t in terr:
+		walk_t.append(1 if t[2] else 0)
+	_wl = 0
+	while _wl < terr.size() and not terr[_wl][2]:
+		_wl += 1
+	water_top = th[_wl - 1] if _wl > 0 else -1.0
+	_land_lo = water_top + 0.012 if _wl > 0 else -0.62
+	if _wl + 1 < terr.size() and terr[_wl][3] == "sand":
+		_land_lo = th[_wl] + 0.012
+	_water = str(pdata.get("water", ""))
+	if _wl == 0:
+		_water = "none"
+	elif _water == "":
+		_water = ["coast", "lake", "river"][posmod(seed_, 3)]
+	_ridge = _noise(seed_, 0.0065, 5, 0.42, FastNoiseLite.TYPE_SIMPLEX_SMOOTH, FastNoiseLite.FRACTAL_RIDGED)
+	_ridge.domain_warp_enabled = true
+	_ridge.domain_warp_amplitude = 30.0
+	_ridge.domain_warp_frequency = 0.01
+	_hills = _noise(seed_ + 1, 0.011, 3, 0.4)
+	_crag = _noise(seed_ + 2, 0.028, 3, 0.45)
+	_bumps = _noise(seed_ + 5, 0.07, 2)
+	_wiggle = _noise(seed_ + 3, 0.008, 3)
+	_meander = _noise(seed_ + 4, 0.007, 1)
+	_meander.fractal_type = FastNoiseLite.FRACTAL_NONE
+	_rn = _noise(seed_ + 6, 0.03, 5)
+	_isle = _noise(seed_ + 21, 0.028, 2, 0.5, FastNoiseLite.TYPE_SIMPLEX_SMOOTH)
+	_n1 = _noise(seed_ + 11, 0.08, 5)
+	_n2 = _noise(seed_ + 12, 0.03, 5)
+	# The water's shape: drawn from the planet's own rng, once.
+	var rng := RandomNumberGenerator.new()
+	rng.seed = seed_ * 7919 + 13
+	match _water:
+		"coast":
+			_coast_dir = Vector2.from_angle(rng.randf() * TAU)
+			for k in rng.randi_range(2, 4):
+				var along := Vector2(-_coast_dir.y, _coast_dir.x) * rng.randf_range(-0.38, 0.38) * N
+				_islets.append([_cen + _coast_dir * rng.randf_range(0.37, 0.44) * N + along, rng.randf_range(6.0, 13.0)])
+		"lake":
+			_lake = {"c": _cen + Vector2.from_angle(rng.randf() * TAU) * rng.randf_range(0.2, 0.3) * N,
+				"r": rng.randf_range(18.0, 30.0), "sq": Vector2(rng.randf_range(0.7, 1.0), rng.randf_range(0.7, 1.0)),
+				"rot": rng.randf() * PI}
+		"river":
+			var u := Vector2.from_angle(rng.randf() * TAU)
+			var fords := []
+			var lat0 := (1.0 if rng.randf() < 0.5 else -1.0) * rng.randf_range(0.2, 0.28) * N
+			for k in 3:
+				fords.append(rng.randf_range(-0.4, 0.4) * N)
+			_river = {"u": u, "side": Vector2(-u.y, u.x), "lat0": lat0, "amp": 0.12 * N, "fords": fords}
+	# The height scale (the relief's range) and the site height (the commonest
+	# walkable band) from a coarse sample of the whole planet.
+	_lo = INF
+	_hi = -INF
+	for i in range(0, N, 8):
+		for j in range(0, N, 8):
+			var v := _relief(i, j)
+			_lo = minf(_lo, v)
+			_hi = maxf(_hi, v)
+	var counts := {}
+	var top_h := -1.0
+	for i in range(0, N, 8):
+		for j in range(0, N, 8):
+			var h := _raw_height(i, j)
+			var t := _band(h)
+			if walk_t[t] == 1:
+				counts[t] = counts.get(t, 0) + 1
+			top_h = maxf(top_h, h)
+	var best := 0
+	var best_n := -1
+	for t in counts:
+		if counts[t] > best_n:
+			best = t
+			best_n = counts[t]
+	var lo: float = th[best - 1] if best > 0 else th[0] - 0.3
+	var hi: float = th[best] if best < th.size() else th[-1] + 0.3
+	site_h = (lo + hi) * 0.5
+	plot_lvl = clampi(floori(maxf(0.0, site_h - water_top - 0.03) / TTILES.TERRACE), 0, 20)
+	if sky:
+		plot_lvl = maxi(plot_lvl, 1)
+	lvl_top = maxi(1, clampi(floori(maxf(0.0, top_h - water_top - 0.03) / TTILES.TERRACE), 0, 20))
+	_height.resize(N * N)
+	_ramp.resize(N * N)
+	_terrain.resize(N * N)
+	_block_done.resize(NB * NB)
+
+
+static func _noise(s: int, f: float, oct := 5, gain := 0.5, type := FastNoiseLite.TYPE_SIMPLEX_SMOOTH, frac := FastNoiseLite.FRACTAL_FBM) -> FastNoiseLite:
+	var n := FastNoiseLite.new()
+	n.seed = s
+	n.noise_type = type
+	n.fractal_type = frac
+	n.fractal_octaves = oct
+	n.fractal_gain = gain
+	n.frequency = f
+	return n
+
+
+func _relief(i: int, j: int) -> float:
+	return 0.62 * _ridge.get_noise_2d(i, j) + 0.38 * _hills.get_noise_2d(i, j)
+
+
+## The water's signed distance at a cell (> 0 land), as SurfaceTerrain draws it.
+func _sd(i: int, j: int) -> float:
+	var p := Vector2(i, j)
+	match _water:
+		"coast":
+			var s := (p - _cen).dot(_coast_dir) - 0.3 * N + N * (0.07 * _wiggle.get_noise_2d(i, j) + 0.015 * _crag.get_noise_2d(i * 2, j * 2))
+			var d := -s
+			for isl in _islets:
+				d = maxf(d, isl[1] * (1.0 + 0.45 * _crag.get_noise_2d(i * 2, j * 2)) - p.distance_to(isl[0]))
+			return d
+		"lake":
+			var lc: Vector2 = _lake["c"]
+			var lsq: Vector2 = _lake["sq"]
+			var q: Vector2 = (p - lc).rotated(float(_lake["rot"])) / lsq
+			return q.length() - _lake["r"] * (1.0 + 0.3 * _wiggle.get_noise_2d(i * 3, j * 3))
+		"islands":
+			var d := (_isle.get_noise_2d(i, j) - 0.08) * 40.0
+			d = maxf(d, 22.0 - p.distance_to(_cen))
+			# (walkways between the platforms: a lattice of them across the sky)
+			var li := posmod(i - N / 2 + BRIDGE / 2, LATTICE) < BRIDGE
+			var lj := posmod(j - N / 2 + BRIDGE / 2, LATTICE) < BRIDGE
+			if li or lj:
+				d = maxf(d, 1.0)
+			d = minf(d, float(mini(mini(i, j), mini(N - 1 - i, N - 1 - j))) - 5.0)
+			return d
+		"river":
+			var q := p - _cen
+			var a := q.dot(_river["u"])
+			var amp: float = _river["amp"]
+			var off: float = _river["lat0"] + amp * _meander.get_noise_1d(a)
+			var slope := amp * (_meander.get_noise_1d(a + 1.0) - _meander.get_noise_1d(a - 1.0)) * 0.5
+			var hw := 3.2 + 1.2 * _crag.get_noise_1d(a * 0.3)
+			var d := absf(q.dot(_river["side"]) - off) / sqrt(1.0 + slope * slope) - hw
+			for f in _river["fords"]:
+				d = maxf(d, (3.0 - absf(a - f)) * 3.0)
+			return d
+	return 1e6
+
+
+func _raw_height(i: int, j: int) -> float:
+	var r := (_relief(i, j) - _lo) / maxf(_hi - _lo, 1e-5)
+	r = pow(clampf(r, 0.0, 1.0), 1.7)
+	var inland := lerpf(_land_lo, 0.8, r) + (0.01 + 0.015 * r) * _bumps.get_noise_2d(i, j)
+	var d := _sd(i, j)
+	var h: float
+	if d <= 0.0:
+		h = lerpf(water_top - 0.015, -0.78, smoothstep(0.0, 10.0, -d))
+	else:
+		h = lerpf(water_top + 0.012, inland, smoothstep(0.0, 30.0, d)) if _wl > 0 else inland
+	return clampf(h, -1.0, 1.0)
+
+
+func _band(h: float) -> int:
+	var t := 0
+	while t < th.size() and h > th[t]:
+		t += 1
+	return t
+
+
+## (worker) The terrain of every block overlapping `r` made (once).
+func ensure(r: Rect2i) -> void:
+	var a := r.intersection(Rect2i(0, 0, N, N))
+	if not a.has_area():
+		return
+	for bx in range(a.position.x / BLOCK, (a.end.x - 1) / BLOCK + 1):
+		for by in range(a.position.y / BLOCK, (a.end.y - 1) / BLOCK + 1):
+			if _block_done[bx * NB + by] == 1:
+				continue
+			_block_done[bx * NB + by] = 1
+			for i in range(bx * BLOCK, mini(bx * BLOCK + BLOCK, N)):
+				for j in range(by * BLOCK, mini(by * BLOCK + BLOCK, N)):
+					var k := i * N + j
+					var h := _raw_height(i, j)
+					_height[k] = h
+					_terrain[k] = _band(h)
+					var rr := smoothstep(0.0, 0.15, _rn.get_noise_2d(i, j))
+					_ramp[k] = maxf(rr, 1.0 - smoothstep(8.0, 14.0, _sd(i, j)))
+
+
+func walkable(c: Vector2i) -> bool:
+	if c.x < 0 or c.y < 0 or c.x >= N or c.y >= N:
+		return false
+	ensure(Rect2i(c, Vector2i.ONE))
+	return walk_t[_terrain[c.x * N + c.y]] == 1
+
+
+func _set_height(c: Vector2i, h: float) -> void:
+	var k := c.x * N + c.y
+	_height[k] = h
+	_terrain[k] = _band(h)
+
+
+func cell_pos(c: Vector2i) -> Vector2:
+	return g2w * Vector2(c)
+
+
+# --- The plan ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+## (worker) The villages, gates, pirates and industry of the whole planet -
+## only the terrain near them is made to plan them.
+func plan() -> void:
+	_rng.seed = seed_
+	var center := Vector2i(N / 2, N / 2)
+	_level_disc(center, 9.0, 14.0)   # the landing site, at the site height
+	_add_clear_spot(center, 3.2)
+	if pdata.get("villages", true):
+		var dir := Vector2.from_angle(_rng.randf() * TAU)
+		_plan_village(center, center + Vector2i(dir * 28.0), true, 0)
+		var vid := 1
+		var quarters := {}   # (a village in every quarter of the planet: the second pass makes sure)
+		var spare := {}
+		for gx in N / REGION:
+			for gy in N / REGION:
+				var vr := RandomNumberGenerator.new()
+				vr.seed = hash([seed_, "village", gx, gy])
+				var c := Vector2i(gx * REGION + REGION / 2, gy * REGION + REGION / 2) + Vector2i(vr.randi_range(-25, 25), vr.randi_range(-25, 25))
+				var qk := Vector2i(gx * 2 / (N / REGION), gy * 2 / (N / REGION))
+				var palace := vr.randf() < 0.35
+				if Vector2(c).distance_to(Vector2(center)) < REGION * 0.8:
+					continue
+				if vr.randf() > VILLAGE_CHANCE:
+					if not spare.has(qk):
+						spare[qk] = [c, palace]
+					continue
+				_rng.seed = hash([seed_, "v", vid])
+				_plan_village(c, c, palace, vid)
+				quarters[qk] = true
+				vid += 1
+		for qk in spare:
+			if not quarters.has(qk):
+				_rng.seed = hash([seed_, "v", vid])
+				_plan_village(spare[qk][0], spare[qk][0], spare[qk][1], vid)
+				vid += 1
+	elif pdata.get("industry", true):
+		_plan_industry()
+	var pr := RandomNumberGenerator.new()
+	pr.seed = hash([seed_, "pirates"])
+	for b in PIRATE_BANDS:
+		var c := Vector2i(pr.randi_range(20, N - 21), pr.randi_range(20, N - 21))
+		if Vector2(c).distance_to(Vector2(center)) < 30.0:
+			continue
+		_rng.seed = hash([seed_, "band", b])
+		_plan_pirate_band(c, pr.randi_range(2, 4))
+	_plan_gates()
+	_plan_village_fauna()
+	planned = true
+
+
+func _plan_village(palace_near: Vector2i, near: Vector2i, palace: bool, vid: int) -> void:
+	village_spots.append(near)
+	var homes: Array = []
+	if palace:
+		var pr := _find_clear_site(Vector2i(16, 14), palace_near, 22)
+		if pr.size != Vector2i.ZERO:
+			_clear_site(pr)
+			var x0 := pr.position.x
+			var y0 := pr.position.y
+			var x1 := pr.end.x - 1
+			var y1 := pr.end.y - 1
+			var cols := []
+			for c in [Vector2i(1, 1), Vector2i(4, 1), Vector2i(1, 11), Vector2i(4, 11),
+					Vector2i(8, 8), Vector2i(12, 8), Vector2i(8, 11), Vector2i(12, 11)]:
+				cols.append([x0 + c.x, y0 + c.y])
+			_add_plan({"rect": [x0, y0, 16, 14], "material": "minoan", "style": "palace", "title": "%s palace" % culture_name,
+				"doors": [[x0 + 3, y1, "sw"], [x1, y0 + 10, "se"], [x0 + 10, y0, "ne"]],
+				"inner": [["i", x0 + 6, y0, y1, y0 + 6], ["j", y0 + 6, x0 + 6, x1, x0 + 10]],
+				"mosaic": [x0 + 1, y0 + 4, 4, 6], "columns": cols})
+	for hi in BUILDINGS.size():
+		var size: Vector2i = [Vector2i(13, 12), Vector2i(12, 12)][hi]
+		var hr := _find_clear_site(size, near, 20)
+		if hr.size == Vector2i.ZERO:
+			continue
+		_clear_site(hr)
+		var door := Vector2i(hr.position.x + size.x / 2, hr.end.y - 1)
+		_add_plan({"rect": [hr.position.x, hr.position.y, size.x, size.y], "material": "minoan", "style": BUILDINGS[hi],
+			"title": "%s %s" % [culture_name, BUILDINGS[hi]], "doors": [[door.x, door.y, "sw"]],
+			"inner": _divider(hr, [[door, "sw"]]), "mosaic": [], "columns": []})
+		homes.append(hr.get_center())
+	_add_clear_spot(near, 4.0)
+	var count := 9 if vid == 0 else 4
+	for k in count:
+		var home := cell_pos(near)
+		var spread := Vector2(120, 60)
+		if k / 2 < homes.size():
+			home = cell_pos(homes[k / 2])
+			spread = Vector2(40, 20)
+		var pos := home + Vector2(_rng.randf_range(-spread.x, spread.x), _rng.randf_range(-spread.y, spread.y))
+		npc_plans.append({"pos": pos, "variant": k + vid * 9, "home": home, "spawned": false, "kind": ""})
+	var ang := _rng.randf() * TAU
+	var dist := _rng.randf_range(30.0, 38.0) if vid == 0 else _rng.randf_range(18.0, 26.0)
+	_plan_pirate_band(near + Vector2i(Vector2.from_angle(ang) * dist), 2 if vid == 0 else 3)
+
+
+func _add_plan(spec: Dictionary) -> void:
+	plans.append({"spec": spec, "built": null})
+	var r := Rect2i(spec["rect"][0], spec["rect"][1], spec["rect"][2], spec["rect"][3])
+	var g := r.grow(3)
+	for i in range(g.position.x, g.end.x):
+		for j in range(g.position.y, g.end.y):
+			plot_cells[Vector2i(i, j)] = true
+
+
+static func plan_rect(p: Dictionary) -> Rect2i:
+	var r: Array = p["spec"]["rect"]
+	return Rect2i(r[0], r[1], r[2], r[3])
+
+
+func _divider(r: Rect2i, doors: Array) -> Array:
+	if r.size.x < 4:
+		return []
+	var door_x: Array = doors.map(func(d): return (d[0] as Vector2i).x)
+	var best := -1
+	var best_w := -1
+	for x in range(r.position.x + 1, r.end.x):
+		if x in door_x:
+			continue
+		var w := mini(x - r.position.x, r.end.x - x)
+		if w > best_w:
+			best_w = w
+			best = x
+	if best < 0 or best_w < 2:
+		return []
+	return [["i", best, r.position.y, r.end.y - 1, r.position.y + r.size.y / 2]]
+
+
+func _find_clear_site(size: Vector2i, near: Vector2i, radius: int) -> Rect2i:
+	var center := Vector2i(N / 2, N / 2)
+	ensure(Rect2i(near - Vector2i(radius, radius) - size, Vector2i(radius, radius) * 2 + size * 2).grow(3))
+	var best := Rect2i()
+	var best_cost := INF
+	for attempt in 90:
+		var pos := near + Vector2i(_rng.randi_range(-radius, radius), _rng.randi_range(-radius, radius)) - size / 2
+		var r := Rect2i(pos, size)
+		var g := r.grow(2)
+		if g.position.x < 5 or g.position.y < 5 or g.end.x > N - 5 or g.end.y > N - 5:
+			continue
+		if g.grow(3).has_point(center) or g.grow(3).has_point(center + Vector2i(1, 1)):
+			continue
+		var ok := true
+		for c in [g.position, Vector2i(g.end.x, g.position.y), g.end, Vector2i(g.position.x, g.end.y)]:
+			if Vector2(c).distance_to(Vector2(center)) > N * 0.5 * 0.82:
+				ok = false
+		for p in plans:
+			if plan_rect(p).grow(4).intersects(r):
+				ok = false
+		if not ok:
+			continue
+		var cost := 0.0
+		for i in range(g.position.x, g.end.x, 2):
+			for j in range(g.position.y, g.end.y, 2):
+				if walk_t[_terrain[i * N + j]] == 0:
+					cost += 4.0
+				cost += absf(_height[i * N + j] - site_h) * 6.0
+		cost += Vector2(r.get_center()).distance_to(Vector2(near)) * 0.15
+		if cost < best_cost:
+			best = r
+			best_cost = cost
+	return best
+
+
+func _clear_site(r: Rect2i) -> void:
+	var g := r.grow(2 + PLOT_EASE)
+	ensure(g)
+	for i in range(maxi(g.position.x, 0), mini(g.end.x, N)):
+		for j in range(maxi(g.position.y, 0), mini(g.end.y, N)):
+			var d := maxi(maxi(r.position.x - i, i - (r.end.x - 1)), maxi(r.position.y - j, j - (r.end.y - 1)))
+			_ramp[i * N + j] = 1.0
+			if d <= 2:
+				_set_height(Vector2i(i, j), site_h)
+			else:
+				_set_height(Vector2i(i, j), lerpf(_height[i * N + j], site_h, 1.0 - smoothstep(2.0, 2.0 + PLOT_EASE, d)))
+
+
+func _level_disc(c: Vector2i, r: float, ease: float) -> void:
+	var R := ceili(r + ease)
+	ensure(Rect2i(c - Vector2i(R, R), Vector2i(2 * R + 1, 2 * R + 1)))
+	for dx in range(-R, R + 1):
+		for dy in range(-R, R + 1):
+			var q := c + Vector2i(dx, dy)
+			if q.x < 0 or q.y < 0 or q.x >= N or q.y >= N:
+				continue
+			var d := Vector2(dx, dy).length()
+			if d > r + ease:
+				continue
+			var k := 1.0 - smoothstep(r, r + ease, d)
+			_set_height(q, lerpf(_height[q.x * N + q.y], site_h, k))
+			_ramp[q.x * N + q.y] = 1.0
+
+
+func _add_clear_spot(cell: Vector2i, radius: float) -> void:
+	clear_spots.append([cell, radius])
+	var rr := radius + 2.0
+	var r := ceili(rr + 3.0)
+	ensure(Rect2i(cell - Vector2i(r, r), Vector2i(2 * r + 1, 2 * r + 1)))
+	for dx in range(-r, r + 1):
+		for dy in range(-r, r + 1):
+			var q := cell + Vector2i(dx, dy)
+			if q.x >= 0 and q.y >= 0 and q.x < N and q.y < N:
+				var k := 1.0 - smoothstep(rr, rr + 3.0, Vector2(dx, dy).length())
+				_ramp[q.x * N + q.y] = maxf(_ramp[q.x * N + q.y], k)
+
+
+func _plan_pirate_band(c: Vector2i, count: int) -> void:
+	var cc := c.clamp(Vector2i(8, 8), Vector2i(N - 9, N - 9))
+	var home := cell_pos(cc)
+	ensure(Rect2i(cc - Vector2i(4, 4), Vector2i(9, 9)))
+	for k in count:
+		var pos := home + Vector2(_rng.randf_range(-160, 160), _rng.randf_range(-80, 80))
+		npc_plans.append({"pos": pos, "variant": _rng.randi_range(0, 9999), "home": home, "spawned": false, "kind": "pirate"})
+
+
+func _plan_industry() -> void:
+	var center := Vector2i(N / 2, N / 2)
+	var kinds := ["refinery", "factory", "depot", "relay"]
+	var rng := RandomNumberGenerator.new()
+	rng.seed = hash([seed_, "industry"])
+	var tries := 0
+	while industry.size() < INDUSTRY_SITES and tries < 400:
+		tries += 1
+		var c := Vector2i(rng.randi_range(12, N - 13), rng.randi_range(12, N - 13))
+		if Vector2(c).distance_to(Vector2(center)) < 24.0:
+			continue
+		if industry.any(func(s): return Vector2(s["cell"]).distance_to(Vector2(c)) < 22.0):
+			continue
+		ensure(Rect2i(c - Vector2i(INDUSTRY_R, INDUSTRY_R), Vector2i(2 * INDUSTRY_R + 1, 2 * INDUSTRY_R + 1)))
+		var ok := true
+		for dx in range(-INDUSTRY_R, INDUSTRY_R + 1):
+			for dy in range(-INDUSTRY_R, INDUSTRY_R + 1):
+				var q := c + Vector2i(dx, dy)
+				if walk_t[_terrain[q.x * N + q.y]] == 0:
+					ok = false
+		if not ok:
+			continue
+		_clear_site(Rect2i(c - Vector2i(INDUSTRY_R - 1, INDUSTRY_R - 1), Vector2i(2 * INDUSTRY_R - 1, 2 * INDUSTRY_R - 1)))
+		for dx in range(-INDUSTRY_R, INDUSTRY_R + 1):
+			for dy in range(-INDUSTRY_R, INDUSTRY_R + 1):
+				plot_cells[c + Vector2i(dx, dy)] = true
+		industry.append({"kind": kinds[industry.size() % kinds.size()], "cell": c})
+
+
+func _plan_gates() -> void:
+	var rng := RandomNumberGenerator.new()
+	rng.seed = hash(planet_id + ":gates")
+	var center := Vector2i(N / 2, N / 2)
+	var spots: Array = [[center, 8, 14]]
+	for v in village_spots:
+		spots.append([v, 10, 22])
+	for k in WILD_GATES * 4:
+		spots.append([Vector2i(rng.randi_range(40, N - 41), rng.randi_range(40, N - 41)), 0, 12])
+	var wild := 0
+	for sp in spots:
+		if gates.size() >= GATE_NAMES.size():
+			break
+		var is_wild: bool = sp[1] == 0
+		if is_wild and wild >= WILD_GATES:
+			continue
+		var cell := _gate_cell(sp[0], sp[1], sp[2], rng)
+		if cell == Vector2i(-1, -1):
+			continue
+		if gates.any(func(g): return Vector2(g["cell"]).distance_to(Vector2(cell)) < GATE_APART):
+			continue
+		gates.append({"cell": cell, "name": "Gate " + GATE_NAMES[gates.size()], "node": null})
+		_add_clear_spot(cell, 2.6)
+		if is_wild:
+			wild += 1
+
+
+func _gate_cell(near: Vector2i, r0: int, r1: int, rng: RandomNumberGenerator) -> Vector2i:
+	ensure(Rect2i(near - Vector2i(r1 + 3, r1 + 3), Vector2i(2 * r1 + 7, 2 * r1 + 7)))
+	for attempt in 60:
+		var a := rng.randf() * TAU
+		var d := rng.randf_range(r0, r1)
+		var c := near + Vector2i(roundi(cos(a) * d), roundi(sin(a) * d))
+		if c.x < 12 or c.y < 12 or c.x > N - 13 or c.y > N - 13:
+			continue
+		if Vector2(c).distance_to(_cen) > N * 0.5 * 0.8 or Vector2(c).distance_to(_cen) < 6.0:
+			continue
+		var ok := true
+		for dx in range(-2, 3):
+			for dy in range(-2, 3):
+				var q := c + Vector2i(dx, dy)
+				if plot_cells.has(q) or not walkable(q):
+					ok = false
+		for p in plans:
+			if plan_rect(p).grow(3).has_point(c):
+				ok = false
+		if ok:
+			return c
+	return Vector2i(-1, -1)
+
