+## The animals that keep to the villages (one herd a village in turn).
+func _plan_village_fauna() -> void:
+	var table: Array = SurfaceCreature.FAUNA.get(tile_set_id, [])
+	var rng := RandomNumberGenerator.new()
+	rng.seed = hash(planet_id + ":fauna")
+	var towns: Array = [Vector2i(N / 2, N / 2)] + village_spots
+	for row in table:
+		if str(row[4]) != "village":
+			continue
+		for g in int(row[1]) * SurfaceCreature.DENSITY:
+			var t: Vector2i = towns[(g + 1) % towns.size()]
+			for attempt in 20:
+				var c := t + Vector2i(Vector2.from_angle(rng.randf() * TAU) * rng.randf_range(10.0, 24.0))
+				if c.x < 4 or c.y < 4 or c.x > N - 5 or c.y > N - 5 or plot_cells.has(c) or not walkable(c):
+					continue
+				_herd(row, c, rng, village_fauna)
+				break
+
+
+func _herd(row: Array, c: Vector2i, rng: RandomNumberGenerator, out: Array) -> void:
+	var home := cell_pos(c)
+	for k in rng.randi_range(int(row[2]), int(row[3])):
+		var pos := home + Vector2(rng.randf_range(-90, 90), rng.randf_range(-45, 45))
+		out.append({"species": str(row[0]), "pos": pos, "home": home, "node": null, "dead": false})
+
+
+# --- A chunk -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+## (worker) Square (cx, cy): its ground arrays, its tiles and map pixels, its animals.
+##   {rect, height, terrain, ramp, lvl, rampd, tiles (level, x, y, source - PackedInt32Array),
+##    map (Image), fauna}
+func chunk(cx: int, cy: int) -> Dictionary:
+	var r := Rect2i(cx * GEN, cy * GEN, GEN, GEN).intersection(Rect2i(0, 0, N, N))
+	var E := r.grow(4).intersection(Rect2i(0, 0, N, N))
+	ensure(r.grow(14))
+	var w := E.size.x
+	var h := E.size.y
+	var walk := PackedByteArray()
+	walk.resize(w * h)
+	var lv := PackedByteArray()
+	lv.resize(w * h)
+	for a in w:
+		for b in h:
+			var i := E.position.x + a
+			var j := E.position.y + b
+			var k := i * N + j
+			var e := a * h + b
+			walk[e] = walk_t[_terrain[k]]
+			if walk[e] == 1:
+				var l := clampi(floori(maxf(0.0, _height[k] - water_top - 0.03) / TTILES.TERRACE), 0, 20)
+				if sky:
+					l = maxi(l, 1)
+				if mini(mini(i, j), mini(N - 1 - i, N - 1 - j)) < 3:
+					l = 0
+				lv[e] = l
+	# Each tile to the commonest level round it (3 x 3), twice: tidy ledges.
+	var cnt := PackedInt32Array()
+	cnt.resize(32)
+	for pass_ in 2:
+		var tmp := lv.duplicate()
+		for a in range(1, w - 1):
+			for b in range(1, h - 1):
+				var e := a * h + b
+				if walk[e] == 0:
+					continue
+				var best := int(lv[e])
+				var best_n := 0
+				for da in [-1, 0, 1]:
+					for db in [-1, 0, 1]:
+						var q: int = (a + da) * h + b + db
+						if walk[q] == 0:
+							continue
+						var v := int(lv[q])
+						cnt[v] += 1
+						if cnt[v] > best_n:
+							best_n = cnt[v]
+							best = v
+				for da in [-1, 0, 1]:
+					for db in [-1, 0, 1]:
+						cnt[lv[(a + da) * h + b + db]] = 0
+				tmp[e] = best if best_n >= 5 else lv[e]
+		lv = tmp
+	# Plots, spots and the landing site flat at the plots' level.
+	for a in w:
+		for b in h:
+			var e := a * h + b
+			if walk[e] == 1 and plot_cells.has(Vector2i(E.position.x + a, E.position.y + b)):
+				lv[e] = plot_lvl
+	for sp in clear_spots:
+		var c0: Vector2i = sp[0]
+		var rad := ceili(float(sp[1]) + 2.0)
+		if not E.grow(rad).has_point(c0):
+			continue
+		var sl := plot_lvl if plot_cells.has(c0) else _level_at(c0)
+		for dx in range(-rad, rad + 1):
+			for dy in range(-rad, rad + 1):
+				var q := c0 + Vector2i(dx, dy)
+				if E.has_point(q) and Vector2(dx, dy).length() <= rad:
+					var e := (q.x - E.position.x) * h + (q.y - E.position.y)
+					if walk[e] == 1:
+						lv[e] = sl
+	var c0 := Vector2i(N / 2, N / 2)
+	for a in w:
+		for b in h:
+			var q := E.position + Vector2i(a, b)
+			if Vector2(q - c0).length() <= 10.0 and walk[a * h + b] == 1:
+				lv[a * h + b] = plot_lvl
+	# Ramps: here and there by nature, then where they link the chunk's ledges.
+	var rd := PackedByteArray()
+	rd.resize(w * h)
+	for a in range(2, w - 2):
+		for b in range(2, h - 2):
+			var e := a * h + b
+			var cell := E.position + Vector2i(a, b)
+			if walk[e] == 0 or hash(cell * 7 + Vector2i(seed_, 3)) % 100 >= 9:
+				continue
+			for rr in range(1, 5):
+				if _ramp_fits(a, b, rr, walk, lv, rd, w, h, cell):
+					rd[e] = rr
+					break
+	_link(r, E, walk, lv, rd, w, h)
+	# What the surface keeps: the chunk's own cells.
+	var out := {"rect": r}
+	var hh := PackedFloat32Array()
+	var tt := PackedByteArray()
+	var rp := PackedFloat32Array()
+	var ll := PackedByteArray()
+	var rr2 := PackedByteArray()
+	var n := r.size.x * r.size.y
+	hh.resize(n); tt.resize(n); rp.resize(n); ll.resize(n); rr2.resize(n)
+	for a in r.size.x:
+		for b in r.size.y:
+			var i := r.position.x + a
+			var j := r.position.y + b
+			var k := i * N + j
+			var e := (i - E.position.x) * h + (j - E.position.y)
+			var o := a * r.size.y + b
+			hh[o] = _height[k]
+			tt[o] = _terrain[k]
+			rp[o] = _ramp[k]
+			ll[o] = lv[e]
+			rr2[o] = rd[e]
+	out["height"] = hh
+	out["terrain"] = tt
+	out["ramp"] = rp
+	out["lvl"] = ll
+	out["rampd"] = rr2
+	out["tiles"] = _tiles(r, E, walk, lv, rd, w, h)
+	out["map"] = _map(r, E, walk, lv, rd, w, h)
+	out["fauna"] = _chunk_fauna(r, cx, cy)
+	return out
+
+
+## A cell's level as a chunk would make it (raw, then the 3 x 3 tidy twice) - for
+## a clear spot whose centre lies in another chunk.
+func _level_at(c: Vector2i) -> int:
+	var E := Rect2i(c - Vector2i(2, 2), Vector2i(5, 5)).intersection(Rect2i(0, 0, N, N))
+	ensure(E.grow(1))
+	var lvls := {}
+	var get_raw := func(q: Vector2i) -> int:
+		var k := q.x * N + q.y
+		if walk_t[_terrain[k]] == 0:
+			return -1
+		var l := clampi(floori(maxf(0.0, _height[k] - water_top - 0.03) / TTILES.TERRACE), 0, 20)
+		if sky:
+			l = maxi(l, 1)
+		return l
+	var cur := {}
+	for i in range(E.position.x, E.end.x):
+		for j in range(E.position.y, E.end.y):
+			cur[Vector2i(i, j)] = get_raw.call(Vector2i(i, j))
+	for pass_ in 2:
+		var nxt := {}
+		for q in cur:
+			if cur[q] < 0:
+				nxt[q] = -1
+				continue
+			var cn := {}
+			var best: int = cur[q]
+			var best_n := 0
+			var full := true
+			for dx in [-1, 0, 1]:
+				for dy in [-1, 0, 1]:
+					var p: Vector2i = q + Vector2i(dx, dy)
+					if not cur.has(p):
+						full = false
+						continue
+					if cur[p] < 0:
+						continue
+					cn[cur[p]] = cn.get(cur[p], 0) + 1
+					if cn[cur[p]] > best_n:
+						best_n = cn[cur[p]]
+						best = cur[p]
+			nxt[q] = best if full and best_n >= 5 else cur[q]
+		cur = nxt
+	return maxi(0, int(cur.get(c, plot_lvl)))
+
+
+func _ramp_fits(a: int, b: int, rr: int, walk: PackedByteArray, lv: PackedByteArray, rd: PackedByteArray, w: int, h: int, cell: Vector2i) -> bool:
+	var d: Vector2i = TTILES.RAMP_DIRS[rr]
+	var side := Vector2i(d.y, d.x)
+	for q in [Vector2i(a, b) + d, Vector2i(a, b) - d, Vector2i(a, b) + side, Vector2i(a, b) - side]:
+		if q.x < 0 or q.y < 0 or q.x >= w or q.y >= h or walk[q.x * h + q.y] == 0:
+			return false
+	var l := lv[a * h + b]
+	var hi := Vector2i(a, b) + d
+	if lv[hi.x * h + hi.y] != l + 1 or rd[hi.x * h + hi.y] != 0:
+		return false
+	for q in [Vector2i(a, b) - d, Vector2i(a, b) + side, Vector2i(a, b) - side]:
+		if lv[q.x * h + q.y] != l:
+			return false
+	return not plot_cells.has(cell)
+
+
+func _step_ok(a: int, b: int, walk: PackedByteArray, lv: PackedByteArray, rd: PackedByteArray, h: int) -> bool:
+	if walk[b] == 0:
+		return false
+	var la := lv[a]
+	var lb := lv[b]
+	var d := Vector2i(b / h - a / h, b % h - a % h)
+	if la == lb:
+		if rd[a] != 0 and _perp(TTILES.RAMP_DIRS[rd[a]], d):
+			return false
+		if rd[b] != 0 and _perp(TTILES.RAMP_DIRS[rd[b]], d):
+			return false
+		return true
+	if lb == la + 1 and rd[a] != 0 and TTILES.RAMP_DIRS[rd[a]] == d:
+		return true
+	if la == lb + 1 and rd[b] != 0 and TTILES.RAMP_DIRS[rd[b]] == -d:
+		return true
+	return false
+
+
+static func _perp(p: Vector2i, q: Vector2i) -> bool:
+	return p.x * q.x + p.y * q.y == 0
+
+
+## Within the chunk: from its biggest stretch of ground, a walk; where it meets
+## land a level up or down it can't reach, a ramp goes in and the walk goes on -
+## every ledge of the chunk linked where a ramp fits (the chunks round link
+## theirs; ground carries over between them at the same level).
+func _link(r: Rect2i, E: Rect2i, walk: PackedByteArray, lv: PackedByteArray, rd: PackedByteArray, w: int, h: int) -> void:
+	var inside := func(e: int) -> bool:
+		var q := E.position + Vector2i(e / h, e % h)
+		return r.has_point(q)
+	var seen := PackedByteArray()
+	seen.resize(w * h)
+	var c0 := Vector2i(N / 2, N / 2)
+	var start := -1
+	if r.has_point(c0):
+		start = (c0.x - E.position.x) * h + (c0.y - E.position.y)
+	else:
+		# (the start: the cell of the chunk's commonest level nearest its middle)
+		var counts := {}
+		for a in range(r.position.x - E.position.x, r.end.x - E.position.x):
+			for b in range(r.position.y - E.position.y, r.end.y - E.position.y):
+				var e := a * h + b
+				if walk[e] == 1:
+					counts[lv[e]] = counts.get(lv[e], 0) + 1
+		var best := -1
+		var best_n := -1
+		for l in counts:
+			if counts[l] > best_n:
+				best_n = counts[l]
+				best = l
+		var mid := Vector2(r.get_center()) - Vector2(E.position)
+		var best_d := INF
+		for a in range(r.position.x - E.position.x, r.end.x - E.position.x):
+			for b in range(r.position.y - E.position.y, r.end.y - E.position.y):
+				var e := a * h + b
+				if walk[e] == 1 and lv[e] == best:
+					var dd := Vector2(a, b).distance_squared_to(mid)
+					if dd < best_d:
+						best_d = dd
+						start = e
+	if start < 0 or walk[start] == 0:
+		return
+	var queue := PackedInt32Array([start])
+	seen[start] = 1
+	var cand := PackedInt32Array()
+	var head := 0
+	var ci := 0
+	while true:
+		while head < queue.size():
+			var c := queue[head]
+			head += 1
+			var a := c / h
+			var b := c % h
+			for q in [c - h if a > 0 else -1, c + h if a < w - 1 else -1, c - 1 if b > 0 else -1, c + 1 if b < h - 1 else -1]:
+				if q < 0 or seen[q] == 1 or walk[q] == 0 or not inside.call(q):
+					continue
+				if _step_ok(c, q, walk, lv, rd, h):
+					seen[q] = 1
+					queue.append(q)
+				elif absi(int(lv[q]) - int(lv[c])) == 1:
+					cand.append(c)
+					cand.append(q)
+		var made := false
+		while ci < cand.size():
+			var a2 := cand[ci]
+			var b2 := cand[ci + 1]
+			ci += 2
+			if seen[b2] == 1:
+				continue
+			var lo := a2 if lv[a2] < lv[b2] else b2
+			var hi := b2 if lo == a2 else a2
+			var d := Vector2i(hi / h - lo / h, hi % h - lo % h)
+			var rr := TTILES.RAMP_DIRS.find(d)
+			if rr <= 0 or rd[lo] != 0 or rd[hi] != 0:
+				continue
+			rd[lo] = rr
+			seen[b2] = 1
+			queue.append(b2)
+			made = true
+			break
+		if not made:
+			break
+
+
+## The chunk's tiles: (level, x, y, source) per tile placed - as PlanetSurface._tile_cells.
+func _tiles(r: Rect2i, E: Rect2i, walk: PackedByteArray, lv: PackedByteArray, rd: PackedByteArray, w: int, h: int) -> PackedInt32Array:
+	var out := PackedInt32Array()
+	var src := {}
+	for i in tile_pieces.size():
+		src[tile_pieces[i]] = i
+	var piece_of := {}
+	for role in ["deep", "shallow", "shore_corner", "shore_left", "shore_right", "block_corner", "block_left", "block_right"] + TTILES.RAMP_PIECES.slice(1) + TTILES.RIMS:
+		var pn := TTILES.pc(tile_set_id, role)
+		if pn != "" and src.has(pn):
+			piece_of[role] = src[pn]
+	var kinds: Array = pdata["terrain"].map(func(t): return t[3])
+	var wet := func(e: int) -> int:
+		return 1 - walk[e]
+	for i in range(r.position.x, r.end.x):
+		for j in range(r.position.y, r.end.y):
+			var a := i - E.position.x
+			var b := j - E.position.y
+			var e := a * h + b
+			var l := int(lv[e])
+			# (water nearby - 2 tiles, the cross - or land nearby, for water)
+			var want: int = 1 - wet.call(e)
+			var near := 0
+			for o in [-2, -1, 1, 2]:
+				if a + o >= 0 and a + o < w and wet.call((a + o) * h + b) == want:
+					near = 1
+				if b + o >= 0 and b + o < h and wet.call(a * h + b + o) == want:
+					near = 1
+			if wet.call(e) == 1:
+				var wrole := "shallow" if near == 1 else "deep"
+				if piece_of.has(wrole):
+					_put(out, 0, i, j, piece_of[wrole])
+				continue
+			if rd[e] != 0:
+				_put(out, l, i, j, piece_of[TTILES.RAMP_PIECES[rd[e]]])
+				continue
+			var low_r := _front_drop(e, i < N - 1 and a < w - 1, e + h, Vector2i(1, 0), l, walk, lv, rd)
+			var low_l := _front_drop(e, j < N - 1 and b < h - 1, e + 1, Vector2i(0, 1), l, walk, lv, rd)
+			if low_r >= 0 or low_l >= 0:
+				var piece := "block_corner" if low_r >= 0 and low_l >= 0 else ("block_right" if low_r >= 0 else "block_left")
+				var bottom := mini(low_r if low_r >= 0 else l, low_l if low_l >= 0 else l)
+				for bb in range(bottom + 1, l + 1):
+					_put(out, bb, i, j, piece_of[piece])
+				continue
+			var water_l: bool = i < N - 1 and a < w - 1 and wet.call(e + h) == 1
+			var water_y: bool = j < N - 1 and b < h - 1 and wet.call(e + 1) == 1
+			var back_l: bool = a > 0 and ((wet.call(e - h) == 0 and int(lv[e - h]) < l) or (sky and wet.call(e - h) == 1)) and rd[e - h] == 0
+			var back_r: bool = b > 0 and ((wet.call(e - 1) == 0 and int(lv[e - 1]) < l) or (sky and wet.call(e - 1) == 1)) and rd[e - 1] == 0
+			if (back_l or back_r) and not water_l and not water_y and piece_of.has("rim_l"):
+				_put(out, l, i, j, piece_of["rim_lr" if back_l and back_r else ("rim_l" if back_l else "rim_r")])
+			elif water_l and water_y and piece_of.has("shore_corner"):
+				_put(out, l, i, j, piece_of["shore_corner"])
+			elif water_y and piece_of.has("shore_left"):
+				_put(out, l, i, j, piece_of["shore_left"])
+			elif water_l and piece_of.has("shore_right"):
+				_put(out, l, i, j, piece_of["shore_right"])
+			else:
+				var pn := TTILES.ground_piece(tile_set_id, kinds[_terrain[i * N + j]], l, near == 1, _n1.get_noise_2d(i, j), _n2.get_noise_2d(i, j))
+				if src.has(pn):
+					_put(out, l, i, j, src[pn])
+	return out
+
+
+static func _put(out: PackedInt32Array, l: int, i: int, j: int, s: int) -> void:
+	out.append(l)
+	out.append(i)
+	out.append(j)
+	out.append(s)
+
+
+func _front_drop(e: int, inside: bool, q: int, d: Vector2i, l: int, walk: PackedByteArray, lv: PackedByteArray, rd: PackedByteArray) -> int:
+	if not inside:
+		return -1
+	if walk[q] == 0:
+		return 0 if sky and l > 0 else -1
+	var lq := int(lv[q])
+	if lq >= l:
+		return -1
+	if rd[q] != 0 and TTILES.RAMP_DIRS[rd[q]] == -d and lq == l - 1:
+		return -1
+	return lq
+
+
+## The chunk's map pixels (the amber console look - PlanetSurface's map).
+func _map(r: Rect2i, E: Rect2i, walk: PackedByteArray, lv: PackedByteArray, rd: PackedByteArray, w: int, h: int) -> Image:
+	var bytes := PackedByteArray()
+	bytes.resize(r.size.x * r.size.y * 3)
+	var tcol: Array = pdata["terrain"].map(func(x): return x[1])
+	var first_land := 0
+	while first_land < walk_t.size() and walk_t[first_land] == 0:
+		first_land += 1
+	for j in range(r.position.y, r.end.y):
+		for i in range(r.position.x, r.end.x):
+			var k := i * N + j
+			var t: int = _terrain[k]
+			var water := walk_t[t] == 0
+			var coast := 0
+			for d: Vector2i in NB4:
+				var q := Vector2i(i, j) + d
+				if q.x < 0 or q.y < 0 or q.x >= N or q.y >= N:
+					continue
+				if (walk_t[_terrain[q.x * N + q.y]] == 0) != water:
+					coast = 2 if absi(d.x) + absi(d.y) == 1 else maxi(coast, 1)
+					if coast == 2:
+						break
+			var c: Color
+			if water:
+				c = MAP_SEA.lerp(MAP_SHALLOW, clampf(float(t) / maxf(1.0, first_land - 1.0), 0.0, 1.0))
+				if i % MAP_GRID == 0 or j % MAP_GRID == 0:
+					c = c.lerp(Color(0.1, 0.35, 0.45), 0.35)
+				if coast > 0:
+					c = c.lerp(Color(0.1, 0.5, 0.65), 0.55 if coast == 2 else 0.25)
+			else:
+				var e := (i - E.position.x) * h + (j - E.position.y)
+				c = MAP_LAND.lerp(tcol[t], 0.42)
+				var l := int(lv[e])
+				c = c.darkened(0.35).lerp(MAP_ELEV_HIGH, 0.75 * float(l) / maxf(1.0, float(lvl_top)))
+				if rd[e] != 0:
+					c = c.lerp(Color(0.95, 0.9, 0.7), 0.6)
+				else:
+					var a := i - E.position.x
+					var b := j - E.position.y
+					for q in [e - h if a > 0 else -1, e + h if a < w - 1 else -1, e - 1 if b > 0 else -1, e + 1 if b < h - 1 else -1]:
+						if q >= 0 and walk[q] == 1 and int(lv[q]) < l:
+							c = c.darkened(0.5)
+							break
+				var hx := _height[mini(i + 12, N - 1) * N + j] - _height[maxi(i - 12, 0) * N + j]
+				var hy := _height[i * N + mini(j + 12, N - 1)] - _height[i * N + maxi(j - 12, 0)]
+				var sh := clampf(-(hx + hy) * 1.6, -1.0, 1.0)
+				if sh > 0.45:
+					c = c.lerp(MAP_LIT, (sh - 0.45) * 0.8)
+				elif sh < 0.0:
+					c = c.darkened(-sh * 0.35)
+				if coast == 2:
+					c = MAP_COAST
+				elif coast == 1:
+					c = c.lerp(MAP_COAST, 0.3)
+			var px := ((j - r.position.y) * r.size.x + (i - r.position.x)) * 3
+			bytes[px] = c.r8
+			bytes[px + 1] = c.g8
+			bytes[px + 2] = c.b8
+	return Image.create_from_data(r.size.x, r.size.y, false, Image.FORMAT_RGB8, bytes)
+
+
+## The chunk's own animals (the wild ones and those found anywhere): its share
+## of the planet's herds, the same every time.
+func _chunk_fauna(r: Rect2i, cx: int, cy: int) -> Array:
+	var out := []
+	var table: Array = SurfaceCreature.FAUNA.get(tile_set_id, [])
+	if table.is_empty():
+		return out
+	var rng := RandomNumberGenerator.new()
+	rng.seed = hash([planet_id, "fauna", cx, cy])
+	var share := float(r.size.x * r.size.y) / float(N * N)
+	var towns: Array = [Vector2i(N / 2, N / 2)] + village_spots
+	for row in table:
+		if str(row[4]) == "village":
+			continue
+		var groups := float(int(row[1]) * SurfaceCreature.DENSITY) * share
+		var n := floori(groups) + (1 if rng.randf() < groups - floorf(groups) else 0)
+		for g in n:
+			for attempt in 12:
+				var c := Vector2i(rng.randi_range(r.position.x, r.end.x - 1), rng.randi_range(r.position.y, r.end.y - 1))
+				if c.x < 10 or c.y < 10 or c.x > N - 11 or c.y > N - 11 or plot_cells.has(c):
+					continue
+				if str(row[4]) == "wild" and towns.any(func(t): return Vector2(t).distance_to(Vector2(c)) < 30.0):
+					continue
+				if Vector2(c).distance_to(_cen) < 8.0 or walk_t[_terrain[c.x * N + c.y]] == 0:
+					continue
+				_herd(row, c, rng, out)
+				break
+	return out
hunks.title: The chunked planet maker
hunks.note: The whole planner: constants, lazily made terrain, the plan, and the per-chunk ground, links, tiles, map and fauna. PlanetSurface runs one of its jobs at a time on a worker and copies the results in.

bubbles.text: The planet's constants, made once: its noise layers, the water's shape (coast, lake, river or islands, drawn from the seed), and the height range and commonest walkable band from a 1-in-8 sample - so no step needs the whole planet.
Terrain is made lazily in 16 x 16 blocks: any code that needs cells calls ensure first, and each block is computed once and kept, with the plan's edits applied on top.
A cell's height from its own coordinates only - ridged noise plus hills, shaped by the distance to the water - so any cell comes out the same whatever order it's made in.

Plans the whole planet's features: the landing disc, the pad's village, a village per 110-tile region by chance (at least one per quarter), pirate bands, gates and village fauna. Each part seeds its own random numbers from the planet's seed, so the plan never depends on what was made before.
Levels a building plot to the site height, easing the ground round it over PLOT_EASE tiles. These edits go into the kept terrain, so every chunk made later sees the flat plot.

bubbles.at: func chunk(cx: int, cy: int) -> Dictionary:
bubbles.text: Makes one 32 x 32 chunk from a 4-tile wider area: ledge levels from the heights, tidied twice by a 3 x 3 majority, plots and clear spots flattened, natural ramps, then links, tiles, map pixels and animals - returned as small arrays the surface copies in.
Works out a cell's level exactly as a neighbouring chunk would, so a clear spot centred in another chunk gets the same level on both sides of the border.
A breadth-first walk from the chunk's main ground; wherever it meets land one level up or down that it can't reach, it puts a ramp there and carries on, until every ledge in the chunk is linked.
Picks the tile piece per cell - water deep or shallow, ramps, block sides where the ground drops, rims, shores, else a ground piece by terrain and noise - as (level, x, y, source) quadruples.
The chunk's minimap pixels: water and coasts, land shaded by its level, ramps lit, ledges darkened and hill-shading from the height slope.

bubbles.at: func _chunk_fauna(r: Rect2i, cx: int, cy: int) -> Array:
bubbles.text: The chunk's share of the planet's wild herds, seeded by the chunk's position so the same animals appear whenever it's made; wild ones keep away from towns.

files.explanation: surface_props.gd holds the things on a planet surface, including the Pilot (the player's automaton). This patch gives the automaton a shield of 40 points (raised by gear's max_shield) that takes hits before health and parts and recharges at 12 a second after 3 s out of the fight. The lander and Minoan NPC pictures now come through ProcArt.sprite, so they show a placeholder until their picture is loaded instead of loading it on the spot.

files.explanation: New: touch controls for phones and tablets (autoload "Touch"). A tap already works as a left click through Godot's mouse emulation; this adds a two-finger tap as a right click, a pinch to zoom, and two columns of on-screen buttons on the left edge for the keys (menu, computer, map, attack, dock, zoom). They show only with a touch screen, in space or on a planet, and not while a menu covers the game.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,151 @@ 
+class_name TouchControls
+extends CanvasLayer
+## On a touch screen (a phone or a tablet - the web build): what the mouse and
+## the keyboard do, by hand (autoload "Touch"). A tap is already the left
+## button (Godot's mouse emulation: fly there, walk there, hold to keep going,
+## hold on a rock to cut it). On top of that:
+##   - a two-finger tap: the right button where the first finger was (scan a
+##     rock, the probe scanner in empty space, the context menu on foot);
+##   - a pinch: zoom (the mouse wheel);
+##   - two columns of buttons by the left edge for the keys: the menu (Esc), the
+##     computer (Tab), the map (M), attack the nearest enemy (F), dock / use
+##     (E), zoom in and out - between the status bars and the event log.
+## Shown only with a touch screen (or `forced`: tests), in play - space and a
+## planet's surface - and not while a menu covers the game (they have their
+## own Close buttons).
+
+const BUTTONS := [["MENU", "pause"], ["COMPUTER", "computer"], ["MAP", "sector_map"], ["ATTACK", "attack"], ["DOCK", "dock"]]
+## Pixels a pinch has to open or close by for one step of zoom.
+const PINCH_STEP := 48.0
+## A two-finger tap: both down for less than this, neither moving more than TAP_SLOP.
+const TAP_TIME := 0.35
+const TAP_SLOP := 24.0
+
+var forced := false
+var _col: GridContainer
+var _touches := {}     # finger index -> position (the viewport's)
+var _starts := {}      # finger index -> [position, time]
+var _pinch_d := 0.0
+var _two_tap := false
+var _check := 0.0
+
+
+func _ready() -> void:
+	layer = 60   # (over the HUD; the menus hide it)
+	process_mode = Node.PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS
+	# Two columns by the left edge, between the status bars and the event log
+	# (the right side has the minimap, the quest and the planet panel).
+	_col = GridContainer.new()
+	_col.name = "Buttons"
+	_col.columns = 2
+	_col.add_theme_constant_override("h_separation", 10)
+	_col.add_theme_constant_override("v_separation", 10)
+	_col.set_anchors_preset(Control.PRESET_CENTER_LEFT)
+	_col.grow_horizontal = Control.GROW_DIRECTION_END
+	_col.grow_vertical = Control.GROW_DIRECTION_BOTH
+	_col.offset_left = 18
+	_col.modulate = Color(1, 1, 1, 0.8)
+	for b in BUTTONS:
+		_col.add_child(_button(b[0], _act.bind(b[1])))
+	_col.add_child(_button("ZOOM +", _wheel.bind(MOUSE_BUTTON_WHEEL_UP)))
+	_col.add_child(_button("ZOOM -", _wheel.bind(MOUSE_BUTTON_WHEEL_DOWN)))
+	add_child(_col)
+	visible = false
+
+
+func _button(text: String, cb: Callable, min_size := Vector2(154, 64)) -> Button:
+	var b := UI.button(text, cb, 20)
+	b.custom_minimum_size = min_size
+	b.focus_mode = Control.FOCUS_NONE
+	return b
+
+
+## A touch screen here? (the web build on a phone or a tablet; a laptop's touch screen too)
+static func available() -> bool:
+	return DisplayServer.is_touchscreen_available()
+
+
+func _process(delta: float) -> void:
+	_check -= delta
+	if _check > 0.0:
+		return
+	_check = 0.25
+	visible = (forced or available()) and in_play() and Keybinds.active_menu() == null and not UI.esc_menu_open()
+
+
+## Space or a planet's surface (not the title screen, Talos, a loading screen).
+func in_play() -> bool:
+	var s := get_tree().current_scene
+	if s == null or s.get_script() == null:
+		return false
+	var p: String = s.get_script().resource_path
+	return p.ends_with("/main.gd") or p.ends_with("/planet_surface.gd")
+
+
+## A key's action, pressed and let go.
+func _act(id: String) -> void:
+	for down in [true, false]:
+		var e := InputEventAction.new()
+		e.action = id
+		e.pressed = down
+		Input.parse_input_event(e)
+
+
+## The mouse wheel at the middle of the screen (zoom).
+func _wheel(button: MouseButton) -> void:
+	var vp := get_viewport()
+	_click(vp.get_visible_rect().size * 0.5, button)
+
+
+## A mouse button pressed and let go at `at` (the viewport's coordinates).
+func _click(at: Vector2, button: MouseButton) -> void:
+	var win := get_viewport().get_final_transform() * at   # (events come in as the window's)
+	for down in [true, false]:
+		var e := InputEventMouseButton.new()
+		e.button_index = button
+		e.pressed = down
+		e.position = win
+		e.global_position = win
+		Input.parse_input_event(e)
+
+
+func _input(event: InputEvent) -> void:
+	if not (forced or available()):
+		return
+	if event is InputEventScreenTouch:
+		var now := Time.get_ticks_msec() / 1000.0
+		if event.pressed:
+			_touches[event.index] = event.position
+			_starts[event.index] = [event.position, now]
+			if _touches.size() == 2:
+				_pinch_d = _span()
+				_two_tap = true
+			elif _touches.size() > 2:
+				_two_tap = false
+		else:
+			if _two_tap and _touches.size() == 2:
+				var first: int = _touches.keys().min()
+				var quick := true
+				for i in _starts:
+					quick = quick and now - float(_starts[i][1]) <= TAP_TIME
+				if quick:
+					_click(_starts[first][0], MOUSE_BUTTON_RIGHT)
+			_two_tap = false
+			_touches.erase(event.index)
+			_starts.erase(event.index)
+	elif event is InputEventScreenDrag and _touches.has(event.index):
+		_touches[event.index] = event.position
+		if _starts.has(event.index) and event.position.distance_to(_starts[event.index][0]) > TAP_SLOP:
+			_two_tap = false
+		if _touches.size() == 2:
+			var d := _span()
+			if absf(d - _pinch_d) >= PINCH_STEP:
+				var mid: Vector2 = (_touches.values()[0] + _touches.values()[1]) * 0.5
+				_click(mid, MOUSE_BUTTON_WHEEL_UP if d > _pinch_d else MOUSE_BUTTON_WHEEL_DOWN)
+				_pinch_d = d
+				_two_tap = false
+
+
+func _span() -> float:
+	var v := _touches.values()
+	return (v[0] as Vector2).distance_to(v[1]) if v.size() >= 2 else 0.0

hunks.note: Builds the button grid, decides when it is visible, and turns touch gestures into the mouse and key events the game already understands, so no other script needed touch-specific code.

bubbles.text: The buttons sit in a two-column grid anchored at the middle of the left edge, between the status bars and the event log.

bubbles.at: visible = (forced or available()) and in_play() and Keybinds.active_menu() == null and not UI.esc_menu_open()
bubbles.text: Checked four times a second: shown only with a touch screen, in play, and with no menu open (menus have their own Close buttons).
A button sends its input action pressed and released, exactly as if the key were tapped.
Each 48 px change in the distance between two fingers sends one mouse-wheel step at the midpoint, so pinching zooms like scrolling.

Its dismantle function, which takes a scene apart a few ms a frame, was made safe: a node out of the tree is just queued for freeing, the pieces start being freed from the next frame, and the node itself is freed at the frame's end. hunks.title: Safe dismantling
hunks.note: Dismantle now avoids freeing anything that might be mid-call or mid-removal: it waits a frame before freeing pieces, stops if the node leaves the tree, and queues the node itself instead of freeing it immediately.

bubbles.text: A node already out of the tree (its parent being removed) is only queued for deletion: freeing its children during that removal was a double free.
The first piece is freed a frame later, because the button or signal that started the dismantle may still be running inside the node.
The node itself is freed at the end of the frame, since it may be the caller (a surface taking itself apart).

files.explanation: New tests for AssetPool, the memory pool for loaded assets. They check that the room is twice the usual need, that nothing is unloaded while it fits, that the least used asset goes first when the pool is full, that held and pinned assets are never unloaded, that each unload is reported and counted, and that ProcArt's sprites are registered in the pool and gain priority when drawn.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,65 @@ 
+extends TestCase
+## The memory pool (AssetPool): loaded assets stay loaded; over budget the
+## least used that nothing holds are unloaded (pinned ones never), each unload
+## noted; the budget twice the usual need; ProcArt's sprites in it; the
+## loading console shows its notes and the pool's total.
+
+var _saved := []
+
+
+func _swap_in() -> void:
+	_saved = [AssetPool._e, AssetPool.used, AssetPool.budget, AssetPool.need, AssetPool.events, AssetPool.serial, AssetPool.unloads, AssetPool.unloaded_bytes, AssetPool.loads, AssetPool.peak]
+	AssetPool._e = {}
+	AssetPool.events = []
+	AssetPool.used = 0
+	AssetPool.unloads = 0
+	AssetPool.unloaded_bytes = 0
+
+
+func _swap_out() -> void:
+	AssetPool._e = _saved[0]
+	AssetPool.used = _saved[1]
+	AssetPool.budget = _saved[2]
+	AssetPool.need = _saved[3]
+	AssetPool.events = _saved[4]
+	AssetPool.serial = _saved[5]
+	AssetPool.unloads = _saved[6]
+	AssetPool.unloaded_bytes = _saved[7]
+	AssetPool.loads = _saved[8]
+	AssetPool.peak = _saved[9]
+
+
+func test_unloads_least_used_only_when_full() -> void:
+	_swap_in()
+	AssetPool.set_need(150)
+	check(AssetPool.budget == 300, "the room is twice the usual need")
+	var gone := []
+	var held := {"busy": true}
+	AssetPool.add("rare", 100, func(): gone.append("rare"))
+	AssetPool.add("common", 100, func(): gone.append("common"))
+	AssetPool.add("busy", 100, func(): gone.append("busy"), func(): return held["busy"])
+	for i in 5:
+		AssetPool.touch("common")
+		AssetPool.touch("busy")
+	check(gone.is_empty() and AssetPool.used == 300, "nothing unloaded while it fits (%d bytes)" % AssetPool.used)
+	check(AssetPool.priority("common") > AssetPool.priority("rare"), "used more, a higher priority")
+	AssetPool.add("pinned", 100, func(): gone.append("pinned"), Callable(), true)
+	check(gone == ["rare"], "over budget: the least used goes first (%s)" % [gone])
+	check(AssetPool.used == 300 and not AssetPool.has("rare"), "and the pool fits again")
+	AssetPool.add("more", 100, func(): gone.append("more"))
+	check(not "busy" in gone and not "pinned" in gone, "never one that's held, nor a pinned one (%s)" % [gone])
+	check(AssetPool.unloads == 2, "unloads counted (%d)" % AssetPool.unloads)
+	var notes: Array = AssetPool.events.filter(func(e): return e[2] == "unload")
+	check(notes.size() == 2 and str(notes[0][1]).begins_with("Unloaded rare"), "each unload reported (%s)" % [notes])
+	check(AssetPool.summary().contains("2 unloaded"), "the total reports them: " + AssetPool.summary())
+	_swap_out()
+
+
+func test_sprites_are_in_the_pool() -> void:
+	ProcArt.get_tex("ship_player")
+	check(AssetPool.has("ship_player"), "a loaded sprite is in the pool")
+	check(AssetPool.budget >= 2 * 200 * 1048576, "room for twice every sprite (%s)" % AssetPool.mb(AssetPool.budget))
+	check(AssetPool.used > 0 and AssetPool.used <= AssetPool.budget, "its total counted: " + AssetPool.summary())
+	var p := AssetPool.priority("ship_player")
+	ProcArt.sprite("ship_player")
+	check(AssetPool.priority("ship_player") > p, "drawing a sprite raises its priority")

files.explanation: New tests for playing by touch (TouchControls, the Touch autoload) and the web build's own settings. They check that the buttons show only in play with a touch screen and step aside under a menu, that COMPUTER opens the Ship Computer, that the zoom buttons and a pinch zoom, and that a two-finger tap acts as the right button. The web checks cover phone text and the anatomy picture paths and regions.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,109 @@ 
+extends TestCase
+## Playing by touch (TouchControls, autoload "Touch": the web build on a phone
+## or a tablet): the buttons for the keys, a pinch to zoom, a two-finger tap
+## for the right button - and the web build's own bits (Settings.on_web).
+
+var _main: Node
+var _was_scene: Node
+
+
+func setup() -> void:
+	Galaxy.new_game(false)
+	SaveGame.travelling = false
+	_was_scene = tree.current_scene
+
+
+func teardown() -> void:
+	Touch.forced = false
+	Touch._touches.clear()
+	Touch._starts.clear()
+	tree.current_scene = _was_scene
+	if is_instance_valid(_main):
+		_main.queue_free()
+	SaveGame.pending = {}
+
+
+func _space() -> void:
+	Galaxy.current_system = Galaxy.HOME
+	_main = load("res://main.tscn").instantiate()
+	tree.root.add_child(_main)
+	tree.current_scene = _main
+	for i in 40:
+		await tree.process_frame
+
+
+func _show() -> void:
+	Touch._check = 0.0
+	await tree.process_frame
+	await tree.process_frame
+
+
+func _touch(index: int, at: Vector2, down: bool) -> void:
+	var e := InputEventScreenTouch.new()
+	e.index = index
+	e.position = at
+	e.pressed = down
+	Touch._input(e)
+
+
+func _drag(index: int, at: Vector2) -> void:
+	var e := InputEventScreenDrag.new()
+	e.index = index
+	e.position = at
+	Touch._input(e)
+
+
+func test_buttons_in_play() -> void:
+	await _show()
+	check(not Touch.visible, "the title screen / no touch screen: hidden")
+	await _space()
+	Touch.forced = true
+	await _show()
+	check(Touch.visible, "in space with a touch screen: shown")
+	var labels: Array = Touch._col.get_children().filter(func(c): return c is Button).map(func(b): return b.text)
+	check(labels.has("MENU") and labels.has("COMPUTER") and labels.has("MAP") and labels.has("ATTACK"), "the keys as buttons (%s)" % str(labels))
+	# The COMPUTER button: Tab - the Ship Computer opens, and the buttons step aside.
+	Touch._act("computer")
+	for i in 10:
+		await tree.process_frame
+	check(_main.ship_menu.visible, "COMPUTER opens the Ship Computer")
+	await _show()
+	check(not Touch.visible, "hidden while a menu covers the game")
+	_main.ship_menu.hide()
+	await _show()
+	check(Touch.visible, "back when it's closed")
+
+
+func test_pinch_and_two_finger_tap() -> void:
+	await _space()
+	Touch.forced = true
+	# The zoom buttons and a pinch: the mouse wheel.
+	_main._zoom = 1.0
+	Touch._wheel(MOUSE_BUTTON_WHEEL_DOWN)
+	await tree.process_frame
+	check(_main._zoom < 1.0, "the - button zooms out (%.2f)" % _main._zoom)
+	var z: float = _main._zoom
+	_touch(0, Vector2(800, 500), true)
+	_touch(1, Vector2(900, 500), true)
+	_drag(1, Vector2(1000, 500))
+	await tree.process_frame
+	check(_main._zoom > z, "fingers apart: zoom in (%.2f -> %.2f)" % [z, _main._zoom])
+	_touch(1, Vector2(1000, 500), false)
+	_touch(0, Vector2(800, 500), false)
+	# A quick two-finger tap in empty space: the right button - the probe scanner.
+	_main.player_data.add_equipment("probe_scanner")
+	_touch(0, Vector2(700, 350), true)   # (empty space: clear of the HUD's panels)
+	_touch(1, Vector2(760, 370), true)
+	_touch(1, Vector2(760, 370), false)
+	_touch(0, Vector2(700, 350), false)
+	for i in 10:
+		await tree.process_frame
+	check(_main.ship_menu.visible and _main.ship_menu.current == _main.ship_menu.MAP_TAB, "a two-finger tap: the right button (the probe scanner's map)")
+
+
+func test_web_bits() -> void:
+	check(not Settings.on_web(), "this isn't a web build")
+	check(Settings.PHONE_TEXT["hud"] > 1.0, "phones start with bigger text")
+	check(AnatomyArt.path("muscles") == "res://art/anatomy/muscles.png", "the full anatomy pictures here")
+	check(ResourceLoader.exists("res://art/anatomy/web/muscles.png"), "the web build's half-size ones exist")
+	check_eq(AnatomyArt.region(Rect2(100, 50, 400, 200)), Rect2(100, 50, 400, 200), "no scaling with the full pictures")

files.explanation: New tool: writes data/sprites/sizes.json, which gives every sprite its size, main colour, shade and the box its opaque part fills. The game uses it to draw a procedural placeholder of the right size, colours and shape before the sprite's picture has loaded. Run it after adding or changing sprites (needs Pillow).

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,34 @@ 
+"""Writes data/sprites/sizes.json: every sprite's pixel size, its two main colours and
+where its opaque part sits - what the game needs to draw a procedural placeholder for a
+sprite before its picture is loaded (PlaceholderArt, ProcArt.sprite).
+  "<key>": [w, h, "rrggbb" (main colour), "rrggbb" (its shade), x0, y0, x1, y1]
+  (x0..y1: the opaque part's box, in hundredths of the width / height)
+Run after adding or changing sprites:  ~/.cache/sa-venv/bin/python tools/sprite_sizes.py
+(needs Pillow)"""
+import json, os
+from PIL import Image
+ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
+DIR = os.path.join(ROOT, "data", "sprites")
+out = {}
+for f in sorted(os.listdir(DIR)):
+    if not f.endswith(".png"):
+        continue
+    im = Image.open(os.path.join(DIR, f)).convert("RGBA")
+    w, h = im.size
+    small = im.resize((max(1, w // 8), max(1, h // 8)), Image.BILINEAR)
+    px = [p for p in small.getdata() if p[3] > 128]
+    if not px:
+        px = [(128, 128, 128, 255)]
+    # The main colour: the opaque pixels' mean; its shade: the mean of the darker half.
+    lum = lambda p: p[0] * 0.3 + p[1] * 0.59 + p[2] * 0.11
+    px.sort(key=lum)
+    def mean(ps):
+        n = len(ps)
+        return "%02x%02x%02x" % tuple(int(sum(p[i] for p in ps) / n) for i in range(3))
+    main = mean(px)
+    shade = mean(px[: max(1, len(px) // 2)])
+    box = im.getchannel("A").point(lambda a: 255 if a > 64 else 0).getbbox() or (0, 0, w, h)
+    out[f[:-4]] = [w, h, main, shade,
+                   int(100 * box[0] / w), int(100 * box[1] / h), int(100 * box[2] / w), int(100 * box[3] / h)]
+json.dump(out, open(os.path.join(DIR, "sizes.json"), "w"), separators=(",", ":"))
+print(len(out), "sprites")
hunks.title: Sprite sizes and colours
hunks.note: Reads every PNG in data/sprites, works out its two main colours from a downscaled copy and its opaque bounding box, and writes them compactly to sizes.json.

bubbles.at: small = im.resize((max(1, w // 8), max(1, h // 8)), Image.BILINEAR)
bubbles.text: Colours are taken from an eighth-size copy: quick, and fine for a placeholder's average colour.
The shade is the mean of the darker half of the opaque pixels, sorted by brightness.

bubbles.at: box = im.getchannel("A").point(lambda a: 255 if a > 64 else 0).getbbox() or (0, 0, w, h)
bubbles.text: The opaque box: pixels with alpha above 64, stored in hundredths of the width and height so the placeholder fits where the real picture's shape is.
